## §3 — Interaction-class taxonomy

Every row block in Parts I–V carries a `class:` from this vocabulary (reconstructed from the slices' shared usage; the definitions below are the ones the mappers and verifiers applied):

- **authorable** — user-owned expression: names, prose, notes, custom-content definitions. Free text is legal ONLY on presentation-effect fields; every authored entry passes the same admission wall regardless of source (finite-semantics law). Recovery is usually per-field revert or compensating rename.
- **structural** — canonical world facts: entity existence, membership, roles, seats, phase/status, save/campaign topology. Changed only through typed operations; the class covers both event-lane structural verbs and store-lane lifecycle ops.
- **actionable** — in-world acts that move the simulation: canon events, impairments and restorations, crises, destruction, party impacts. The archetype carries predicate gating, exact preview, receipts, and snapshot- or scrub-undo.
- **influenceable** — derived facts, never directly writable (determinism law: a seed is a world, forever). Rows of this class invert `reach` into TRACED INPUT CAUSES — the legal upstream levers. Any surface that displays one without a why-trace is an `influenceable-without-why` gap.
- **presentational** — view-only or cosmetic state with no simulation consequence: map edits, fog, lenses, prefs, overlays, teaching chrome, export actions. "Cosmetic-always, no canon lock."
- **immutable-evidence** — append-only records and receipts: the event log, chronicle, snapshots, wizardNews, pipeline receipts, ratified design docs. Annotatable at most, never rewritable; an op that silently destroys one (e.g. `uncanonize` wiping the eventLog) is a doctrine-conflict finding.
- **inspect-only** — read-only substrate and authority surfaces: schema manifests, vocabulary modules, enforcement tests/walkers, hidden data seams. Recorded because they are the LAW other rows cite, not because a user acts on them.

Verifiers extended the vocabulary in place where reality demanded it: **prohibited-by-honesty** (custom-content), **declared-but-inert** (narrative-evidence), **live-twin** and **generation-frozen influenceable** (derived-influenceable), and the maturity classes **dead-code**, **flag-off**, and **unwired** (a module with zero production importers — distinct from flag-off; presentation-scene pass 2). These appear in rows exactly as the slices wrote them.

**[amended-by-critic-pass — lever-field normalization rule for `class: influenceable`.]** The canonical lever field is **`traced input causes`**. Three slice spellings exist for the same semantic field: derived-influenceable writes `reach (TRACED INPUTS = levers):` / `reach (TRACED INPUTS):` — and, per its own preamble, its subsequent bare `reach:` lines ARE lever lines under the declared inversion; power-faith writes `inputs (traced levers, the inverted reach field):` with NO `reach:` line at all; economy-family writes `traced input causes:` AND keeps separate `reach:` lines that carry DOWNSTREAM DISPLAY CONSUMERS — the opposite of the inversion this section declares. Normalizers must treat any `reach:` line on an economy-family influenceable row as display-consumer data, never as levers. Full statement: CONFLICT 4 (§5); census of influenceable rows carrying no lever field at all: gap #172b (VI.12).

**[corrected-by-R-4-P5 — the normalization above is DEFERRED, NOT APPLIED, and two of its instructions are wrong as written.]** Wave R-4 lane P-5 enumerated the field across the whole file before normalizing, and stopped. **Denominator: 107 row blocks carry `class: … influenceable`** (108 raw `- class:` lines; the `healthPip + needsAttention` cluster at L9745 carries two), across 10 slices, spelled **18 distinct ways** (plus 5 rows carrying no lever-ish field under any spelling). Two corrections to the rule above, both executed against this file:

1. **"its subsequent bare `reach:` lines ARE lever lines" is FALSE for 2 of the 17** bare `- reach:` lines in derived-influenceable. Fifteen sit on the class-less causal-variable sub-rows (levers — the rule is right there). **Two sit on `class: inspect-only` rows — `FROZEN_VS_LIVE` (L10292) and `ENGINE_FIELD_REGISTRY` (L10303) — where `reach:` carries genuine downstream consumers.** Those two rows were appended by the same critic pass that wrote this rule, which was never re-scoped to its own additions. A normalizer applying the rule verbatim would relabel the field-law authority's consumer data as "traced input causes".
2. **`inputs:` is not a lever spelling in general.** It is the atlas's **universal row-schema field, present on every class in all 15 slices** (~400 occurrences). derived-influenceable fills it `inputs: n/a (derived)` on the very rows whose levers live in `reach (TRACED INPUTS)`. The same field name therefore carries op-inputs in one slice and levers in another; renaming it on influenceable rows alone would fork the shared row schema along a class boundary.

**Four semantic families, not three spellings** (this is why the fork is not orthographic):

| Family | Slices | Lever field | what `reach:` means there |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — dual/hybrid | tabs-read-a/-b, presentation-scene, npc-family, store-ops-a, custom-content, narrative-evidence | `inputs*:` | **hybrid** — causes and display-consumers in ONE prose sentence (6 of 33 tabs-read-a rows measurably both) |
| B — lever-only | power-faith | `inputs (levers):` | field absent |
| C — clean split | economy-family | `traced input causes:` | display consumers |
| D — inverted | derived-influenceable | `reach (TRACED INPUTS*):` | levers, while `inputs:` = `n/a (derived)` |

**Why it was not mechanized** (any one of these defeats a field rename): the 16 causal-variable sub-rows inherit `class: influenceable` from an **inline pipe-separated shared preamble** (L9783, `- class: influenceable · operations: … · inputs: n/a · …`) that no line-anchored field regex can see, and carry no per-row `class:` line — so a rule scoped to `class: influenceable` misses the single largest concentration of lever data in the atlas; family A's hybrid lines would need prose SPLIT, not relabelled, which rewrites verified audit findings; and `reach` means levers and consumers on different rows of the SAME slice. Normalizing is therefore a **semantic re-adjudication of 107 verified rows**, which §5's standing merge rule reserves ("BOTH claims are kept … not adjudicated") and which the Part headers' verbatim guarantee forbids. **Owner ruling required** — recorded in docs/CAPABILITY_REMEDIATION_PLAN.md (Wave R-4, lane P-5). Note for whoever takes the ruling: gap #172b's "the census cannot be pinned until the canonical spelling is normalized" is itself **too optimistic** — P-5's independent fourth run (107 rows / 5 with no lever-ish field under ANY spelling) produced yet another number, because the spread is driven by what counts as a lever FIELD, not by how it is spelled. Normalizing the spelling would freeze one reading of the semantics rather than settle it. This paragraph amends synthesized front matter only; **no embedded slice body was touched.**

## §5 — Cross-slice CONFLICT register

Per the merge rules, where two slices disagree about the same subject BOTH claims are kept, side by side, flagged CONFLICT — not adjudicated. Three genuine cross-slice disagreements survived assembly (in-slice disagreements that a verifier pass already resolved are not repeated here; they stand resolved inside their slices) **[amended-by-critic-pass: now four — CONFLICT 4, a schema fork rather than a fact dispute, added below]**:

**CONFLICT 1 — regen-edit-loss on the NPC branch: FIXED vs STILL-LIVE.**
- Claim A (slice npc-family, headline verification, CONFIRMED by mapper + both verifiers, end-to-end re-derivation + real-pipeline test `tests/generators/regenPreservesUserCanon.test.js:83`; concurred by tabs-read-b gap 12 and lifecycle-recovery Part (b)): the hazard is **FIXED in this tree** for the NPC branch — `regenNPCsPipeline` runs a preservation tail (`mergePreservedNpcs` → `preservesEntity` → `_authored ⇒ canon ⇒ preserved`, in the UNTRACKED `src/domain/regenerationPreservation.js`), so an edited NPC survives an NPC reroll and the EditableText tooltip promise is now true. History branch remains destructive (documented owner-gated deferral).
- Claim B (slice store-ops-a `applyUserEditAction` row; slice store-ops-b `regenSection` row; slice workbench-current gap 5; slice commands-surveyor pending-edits notes): **HAZARD:regen-edit-loss** — `regenSection('npcs')` durably destroys `_userEdits`/`_authored` while the Edit tooltip promises reroll survival. These slices carry it from recorded memory, explicitly labelled PLAUSIBLE / not re-verified this session (store-ops-b wrote CONFIRMED sourced to memory).
- Why it matters: the fix lives in UNTRACKED files; on the committed lineage Claim B is still true. Any consumer of this atlas must know which lineage it is standing on. Not adjudicated here.

**CONFLICT 2 — `destroySavedSettlement` exposure: Timeline.jsx vs zero UI callers.**
- Claim A (slice store-ops-a, K-A row): `exposure: settlement/Timeline.jsx`.
- Claim B (slice composer-verbs, DESTROY_SETTLEMENT row + gap 11, grep-verified): **no component calls it in the current tree** — the only references are the operation registry, the generated compendium row, and Timeline's flat-log-row SHAPE COMMENT (Timeline.jsx:79-85 documents the shape; it does not invoke the op). Registry-only reachability.
- Both slices agree on the substance that matters (a second, confirm-free, pipeline-free, undo-free DESTROY_SETTLEMENT writer exists); they disagree on whether Timeline is a caller. Not adjudicated.

**CONFLICT 3 — the `surveyor:` column on K-B ops dispatched from Surveyor panels.**
- Claim A (slice store-ops-a, preamble + rows, e.g. `setActiveSaveId`, `updateSavedCampaign`, corpus trio): `surveyor: none` for every op outside the two `applyDispatch` targets — "Every other op in this population: surveyor=none, structurally."
- Claim B (slice store-ops-b, corrected preamble census `grep -rn "useStore(" src/components/surveyor/*.jsx`; slice commands-surveyor, exposure-ruleset caveat, independently re-confirmed): **live Surveyor panels dispatch registered K-B ops directly, outside the command plane** — ConstructionPanel (`instantWorld`, `setActiveSaveId`), AutonomyPanel (`advanceCampaignWorld`, `injectCampaignStressor`, `updateSavedCampaign`), StyleOverhaulPanel (`applyMapEdit`), CorpusFactoryPanel (`stageCorpusCandidates`/`reviewCorpusCandidate`/`removeCorpusCandidate`) — deterministic, human-clicked, no command envelope, no provenance stamp.
- The claims are reconcilable as scope (structural routability vs live panel dispatch) but as written they contradict on specific rows' `surveyor:` values. Normalizers must follow the commands-surveyor SURVEYOR EXPOSURE RULESET (Part II.D), which carries the caveat. Not adjudicated.

**CONFLICT 4 — the influenceable lever-field schema fork (SCHEMA, not fact). [amended-by-critic-pass]**
- Three slices spell the influenceable class's lever field three different ways, and one of them re-uses a field name the others inverted. Derived-influenceable: `- reach (TRACED INPUTS = levers):` / `- reach (TRACED INPUTS):`, with its preamble declaring "The `reach` field is INVERTED per the brief: it lists the TRACED INPUT CAUSES (the legal levers)" — so even its later bare `- reach:` lines are lever lines. Power-faith: `- inputs (traced levers, the inverted reach field):` (2 rows, e.g. Public legitimacy) with NO `- reach:` line at all. Economy-family: `- traced input causes:` / `- traced input causes (the levers):` (11 rows) AND separate `- reach:` lines that carry DOWNSTREAM DISPLAY CONSUMERS (e.g. the activeChains row: `reach: EconomicsTab Economic Flows section … ServicesTab per-service chain-depth badges …`) — the OPPOSITE of §3's declared inversion. A fourth minor variant exists in tabs-read-a (`- inputs: (influenceable) traced input causes:`, the warfaith.faith-panel row).
- No slice is wrong about facts. But a normalizer that reads `reach` as levers uniformly will mis-read every economy-family influenceable row (display consumers become "legal levers"), and one that reads `reach` as consumers uniformly will mis-read all of derived-influenceable. Canonical field going forward: **`traced input causes`** (§3 normalization rule, added by this pass). Census of the rows carrying no lever field under ANY spelling: gap #172b (VI.12). CONFIRMED (all spellings located and read this session).
- **[RULED — owner, 2026-07-27, over the R-4 P-5 three-option menu: OPTION 1 RATIFIED.** The slices stay verbatim; §3's corrected rule is the reader's decoder ring; `traced input causes` remains aspirational vocabulary, never a retro-normalization; gap #172b stays open BY CONSTRUCTION. Options 2 (re-adjudicate all 107 rows) and 3 (partial normalize) are retired.] **[corrected-by-R-4-P5] STATUS history: the cure was attempted in Wave R-4 (lane P-5) and DEFERRED to an owner ruling — now ruled above.** The full enumeration, the four-family table, and two corrections to the §3 rule live in §3 (read them before any future normalization attempt). Headline corrections: "three slices / three spellings" is really **four semantic families and 18 spellings over 107 influenceable rows**; `inputs:` is the atlas's universal row-schema field, not a lever spelling; and the instruction that derived-influenceable's bare `- reach:` lines are all lever lines is **false for 2 of 17** — `FROZEN_VS_LIVE` (L10292) and `ENGINE_FIELD_REGISTRY` (L10303) are `class: inspect-only` rows whose `reach:` carries consumers. Normalizing is a semantic re-adjudication of verified rows, not a rename, so it is barred by this register's own "not adjudicated" rule and by the Part headers' verbatim guarantee.

The legend at 337-340 has the same hole: its second entry is `['','#2d7a44','Force-added by you']`, which renders as a zero-width coloured span followed by literal " = Force-added by you". Legibility-law candidate for the G-0 purge; one-string fix (give `forced` a glyph).

## Subject: DeityAssignmentPanel — `src/components/settlement/DeityAssignmentPanel.jsx`

**The only write surface in half A.** Mounted under the Power tab, editable dossiers only: `{!readOnly && <DeityAssignmentPanel/>}` (OutputContainer.jsx:677-687). Placement rationale in-code: "deity assignment props/erodes the ruler's legitimacy, so it belongs with governance."

**[added-by-verifier-2 — SECOND MOUNT, outside the dossier.]** This component is NOT dossier-exclusive. `grep -rn "DeityAssignmentPanel" src` returns a second live mount chain: `src/components/map/HeraldBody.jsx:39` lazy-imports `AssignDeityFromMap` and mounts it at **HeraldBody.jsx:193** inside the Herald's `faith` section (beside `PantheonPanel`), and `AssignDeityFromMap.jsx:27` imports and renders **the same `DeityAssignmentPanel`** after `hydrateFromSave` loads the chosen campaign settlement into the live detail slot (its header states the flow verbatim at AssignDeityFromMap.jsx:100-111). A third path stages the same two canon events without this panel at all: the Event Composer (`eventComposer/buildEvent.js:172-203`, `EventComposer.jsx:247`, `EventComposerDeityField.jsx`). Consequence: every "the panel mounts only under Power / the wizard editor is the sole exposure" claim in this slice is **dossier-scoped only**, and the two gap entries that generalised it are corrected below. (The extra surfaces are out of this slice's population — but the gap statements were not scoped, and as written they were false.)

### deity.patron-assignment (assign / clear the settlement's patron deity)
- class: structural — canonical world fact changed via a typed operation
- authority: `settlement.config.primaryDeityRef` + `config.primaryDeitySnapshot` (frozen embed); truth committed by the pure mutate.js SET_PRIMARY_DEITY handler **[amended-by-critic-pass: the bare name "mutate.js" resolves to `src/domain/events/mutate.js:108` (registry entry `SET_PRIMARY_DEITY: setPrimaryDeity`; `IMPOSE_CULT: imposeCult` is :109) [recheck corrected an off-by-one against the live tree]. There is NO `src/store/mutate.js` — this slice's pass-2 Verification correction (5) already refutes that path; annotated here at the row body so the bare name cannot be mis-resolved to the store. Re-confirmed against the live tree this pass.]**
- operations: `setPrimaryDeity(refId)` → `setPrimaryDeityImpl` (settlementDeityHelpers.js:63-88) → `state.applyEvent({type:'SET_PRIMARY_DEITY', targetId, payload:{deityRef, snapshot}})`; clear via falsy ref (helpers:67-73). UI: `<select data-testid="patron-deity-select">` with "No patron (latent)" option (panel:175-184)
- inputs: a `custom:<localUid>` deity ref from `buildRegistry(customContent).listCustom('deities')` — embedded identity is the minted account-scoped `deity:<scope>:<slug>` (helpers:27-34, cross-account collision fix)
- preconditions: settlement present; premium/elevated `canUseCustomContent()` for the write picker (panel:93, tier matrix in header 17-21); unknown ref ⇒ refuse, null return, no event (helpers:80); free user who somehow dispatched is inert — "can't advance time, so the assignment is inert (D.0)" (helpers:56-57)
- timing: immediate (canon event applied to the live settlement)
- scope: settlement (config field pair)
- reach: subsystemActivation flips the religion gate the instant a member carries the snapshot (helpers:10-12); pulse + derivers read ONLY the embedded snapshot, never the store (headless-determinism contract); FaithSection ACTIVE mode keys off the same embed (FaithSection.jsx:276); WarFaith tab PRESENCE keys off it (OutputContainer.jsx:481-482); legitimacy divine-mandate coupling
- preview: none — no cascade preview of what assigning a patron will do to legitimacy/faith before committing

It CAN be changed from the Realm: HeraldBody.jsx:193 → AssignDeityFromMap → the same panel, for any settlement in the active campaign. The defect is therefore a *navigation* defect (the op lives on a different surface than the facts it changes, and the dossier gives no pointer to it), not an unreachable operation; (2) DEITY DOCTRINE verified: options come exclusively from `registry.listCustom('deities')` (panel:96-99) — NO premade pool anywhere in the path; empty library ⇒ "none authored" copy, never a stock list (panel:171-172); (3) lapsed tier gets the read-only owned view + renew prompt, free gets the upsell naming NO deity (panel:111-152) — reads `config.primaryDeitySnapshot` only, never `config.latentPantheon` (header:19-21)

- **operations** (all with source): (1) Event Composer single Apply — `EventComposer.jsx:368-419` → store `applyEvent` (`settlementSlice.js:1579`); (2) "+ Add to batch" → BatchCart apply — `EventComposer.jsx:733,753-775` → `applyEventBatch` (`settlementSlice.js:1881`, replays through the single-event path); (3) §10 mutable docket — re-stage an already-queued intention in place (`updateQueuedEvent`, `EventComposer.jsx:389-394`); (4) Surveyor/AI command lane — `settlement.canon-event.apply` (`src/application/commands/adapters/canonEventApply.js:36-70`, `surveyor: true`), which calls the SAME `settlementSlice.applyEvent` writer. **Four more lanes exist and are NOT composer-standard** [added-by-verifier]: (5) the clock-bound tick replay, `drainQueuedEvents` (a mutation lane; covered under *timing* below); (6) `counterfactual()` (counterfactual.js:187-192), a READ-ONLY what-if that runs `runEventPipeline` on hand-built REMOVE_INSTITUTION / DAMAGE_INSTITUTION / ADD_INSTITUTION / KILL_NPC events with no manifest predicate — see Gaps #12; (7) **the deity store lane** — `setPrimaryDeity` / `imposeCult` (settlementSlice.js:2166-2167 → `settlementDeityHelpers.js` `setPrimaryDeityImpl` :65-89 / `imposeCultImpl` :104-152) construct SET_PRIMARY_DEITY / IMPOSE_CULT events in the STORE and dispatch them through the SAME `state.applyEvent` writer, driven by a second UI (`<DeityAssignmentPanel />`, mounted at OutputContainer.jsx:686 and again inside AssignDeityFromMap.jsx:97 ← HeraldBody.jsx:193) — no manifest predicate, no composer preview, no batch, no docket — see Gaps #14 [added-by-verifier-2]; and (8) `contentSampleCategoryFixtures.js:292-300`, a second READ-ONLY producer (domain `applyEvent`, no timestamp, no store) that runs SET_PRIMARY_DEITY / ADD_FACTION / APPLY_STRESSOR for the custom-content taste gate — see Gaps #12 [added-by-verifier-2]. One verb (DESTROY_SETTLEMENT) additionally has a second, wholly separate WRITER outside this list — see its row and Gaps #11.
- **preconditions (global)**: manifest predicate must pass (`EventComposer.jsx:255-264` — unavailable verbs render grayed-with-reason, disabled in the select at :459-466); `canonEventCommandFence` blocks applies while a canon command is in flight (`settlementSlice.js:1584-1604`); target required when `spec.requiresTarget`. Phase: both draft and canon are legal (`EventComposer.jsx:2-9`).
- **timing**: immediate in draft and in unbound canon; **next-pulse** when the settlement is clock-bound to a canonized campaign — the event queues (`queueSettlementEvent`, `settlementSlice.js:1620-1648`) and resolves simultaneously at the next advance via `drainQueuedEvents` (`src/domain/events/drainQueuedEvents.js:1-35`), which re-runs the same veto channel at the tick (`refusals` array declared at :33/:68 and pushed at :95 `missing_target`/`target_inactive`, :126 `malformed`, :128-140 the handler veto) [corrected-by-verifier-2: was ":1-25", which is the header comment and stops BEFORE the refusals contract at :33 — evidence src/domain/events/drainQueuedEvents.js:33,68,95,126,133]. Queue refusals (`advance_in_flight`/`advance_paused`) surface as blocking, form-keeping refusals (`settlementSlice.js:1626-1645`; `EventComposer.jsx:398-407`).
- **preview**: **exact** — preview and apply run the identical `runEventPipeline` ("what the preview promised is exactly what the apply delivers", `applyEvent.js:4-8`); live preview re-derives the full pipeline on every form change, 150ms debounce (`EventComposer.jsx:292-307`); staleness law keys the pane to payload-hash × settlement reference (`settlementSlice.js:1555-1561`). **Degrades to deterministic-scope when clock-bound**: the pane is labeled isolated-scope review — "earlier queued orders and intervening world changes may alter the eventual result" (`PreviewPanel.jsx:12-14,72`). This is the SED-13/SED-16 distinct-language contract, present today.
- **persistence**: store `settlement` + `systemState`; canon-only `eventLog` append (`settlementSlice.js:1754-1756`); durable save via `updateSavedSettlement` + `persistSaveUpdate` (`settlementSlice.js:1774-1788`) → outbox → Supabase when configured, anonymous/local library otherwise, mirrored to localStorage (`src/store/campaignSliceShared.js:360-378`).
- **recovery**: **snapshot-undo** in canon — `undoLastEvent` (`settlementSlice.js:1949`) restores systemState from the log entry, scrubs provenance-tagged writes, and restores non-reversible records from the pre-event snapshot `applyEvent` stamps on the entry (`undoEvent.js:1-130`; per-verb snapshot keys noted per row). UI exposure: Timeline's undo, **latest entry only, and not while clock-bound** (`Timeline.jsx:70`). Queued (clock-bound) intentions are removable/editable in the docket before the tick (`PendingIntentions.jsx`). **Draft-phase applies write no eventLog entry → no undo path** (see Gaps). **Taxonomy warning** [added-by-verifier-2]: "snapshot-undo" is used below as the umbrella name for `undoLastEvent`, but only 26 of the 40 types actually get a pre-event snapshot. `captureEventUndoSnapshot` returns **null** for every type absent from `SNAPSHOT_CONFIG_KEYS` (undoEvent.js:64-98) and `SNAPSHOT_SETTLEMENT_KEYS` (undoEvent.js:130-215) — including **IMPAIR_INSTITUTION, IMPAIR_FACTION, EXPOSE_CORRUPTION's veto path, DESTROY_SETTLEMENT, CHANGE_RULING_POWER's non-powerStructure writes, and every fold with no map row**. Those verbs recover by **provenance scrub only** (causeEventId impairment strip + `scrubUndoneEvent`'s five provenance passes, undoEvent.js:488-499). Rows that name specific snapshot keys have been re-derived against those two maps; rows that say bare "snapshot-undo" are the umbrella term and should be read as "undoLastEvent", not as "a pre-event copy exists". The G-2b matrix must not collapse the two — they have different failure modes.
- **provenance**: canon EventLogEntry with event, appliedAt, beforeState/afterState, deltas, causalStateDeltas, factionResponses, narrativeSummary (`applyEvent.js:49-63`); ActionResult envelope with an 'event' Receipt + persistenceOps (`settlementSlice.js:1813-1832`); analytics `EVENT_EDIT_APPLIED` (event_type enum only — `settlementSlice.js:1796-1801`). Draft applies: none (see Gaps).
- **exposure (TODAY)**: SettlementDetail's "Make Changes" panel — the sole mount, `SettlementDetail.jsx:643` (`<EventComposer />`); entry paths inside it: verb dropdown (grayed-with-reason), ComposerNavigator's pressures rail (≤3, `affordanceManifest.js:713-759`), target-first entity→verb chips, family browse, and search (`ComposerNavigator.jsx:73-216`); intents also staged from outside via `stageComposerIntent` (SuccessorPrompt.jsx:66,86; PendingIntentions.jsx:125 docket-edit). The EventComposer *component* has exactly one mount (verified by grep for `<EventComposer`), but the verb ROSTER has a second read surface: the Library glossary generates an entry per authorable verb (`glossary.js:35,160`) — see Gaps #13. [added-by-verifier] **"Sole mount" is true of the component, NOT of verb exposure in a second sense either**: two authorable verbs (SET_PRIMARY_DEITY, IMPOSE_CULT) are also authored from `<DeityAssignmentPanel />` — a wholly separate WRITE surface on the dossier (OutputContainer.jsx:686) and on the map/Herald (AssignDeityFromMap.jsx:97 ← HeraldBody.jsx:193). See those rows and Gaps #14. [added-by-verifier-2]
- **destination (G-2b recommendation)**: **contextual-tool** — the composer is already target-first; its verbs should surface as the Workbench's contextual actions on the selected entity, keeping ONE mutation path (the Workbench shell deliberately adds no second one today — `SettlementWorkbench.jsx:10-15`).
- **surveyor**: stage/execute via the reviewed command lane only (`canonEventApplySpec.surveyor: true`, `standardCommandRegistry.js:19-26`); the command carries a TYPED event (enum type + reference targets + banded dials) so finite-semantics holds — AI is a bucketing clerk; the only free text is the presentation-only `description` field (`buildEvent.js:222`). No autonomous apply; same veto channel refuses illegal orders.
- **maturity**: built. **status**: CONFIRMED (file read this session).

## Realm-verb lane — the four settlement-scoped `REALM_MANIFEST` verbs **[added-by-critic-pass]**

Out-of-population ADDENDUM — the slice's 40/40 arithmetic below is untouched. The Denominator ledger records the 14 `realmManifest.js` verbs as "a sibling manifest, explicitly a separate population", and verifier-2 ruled their worldPulse literals out of the composer census ("not registry types — realm/lifecycle lane, out of population"). That boundary call was correct for the AFFORDANCE_MANIFEST denominator, but four of the 14 are settlement-scoped, DM-reachable, settlement-FATE verbs — one of them a settlement-terminal-death writer — and an atlas of the settlement's operation surface that omits them under-reports it. They are rowed here, marked as the addendum they are.

**Declared boundary for the other 10 (BY SCOPE, not silently dropped — see also the §4 denominators row):** DECLARE_CASUS / SUE_FOR_PEACE / ORDER_SUPPLY_RAID / DECLARE_TRADE_EMBARGO carry explicit `scope:'realm'` (realmManifest.js:211,229,244,260); ORDER_INTERVENTION / REINFORCE / INTERCEPT / ORDER_CONVOY / DECLARE_BLOCKADE / FORCE_RECONSIDERATION are realm-actor war/naval/momentum verbs whose parked factory shapes declare scope `'realm'` (navalKernel.js:509,521; momentum.js:1075; convergence.js:1337,1350,1363) **[amended-by-critic-pass recheck: the earlier `'regional'` claim cited convergence.js:1276, a wizard_news literal, not a verb factory — all three convergence factories declare `'realm'`]**. Two of those ten (REINFORCE, INTERCEPT) are additionally lane-`'deferred'` — registered, not executable ("a documented W-CONVERGENCE deferral", realmManifest.js:449-450).

**Shared substrate — "realm-proposal-standard" (referenced by all four rows).** The DM picks the verb in `RealmVerbComposer` (`src/components/map/RealmVerbComposer.jsx` — the verb list is built from `realmVerbs()` at :71, i.e. ALL 14 including dark/deferred entries with their veto prose; staging goes through the registered store action `stageRealmVerb`, bound at :54, called at :101), mounted TWICE: the Herald's Adjudication desk (`src/components/map/HeraldAdjudication.jsx:22,651`) and the World Pulse panel (`src/components/map/WorldPulsePanel.jsx:27,317`). `stageRealmVerb` (campaignWorldPulseSlice.js:616-631; registered at operationRegistry.js:107, klass `macro`, receiptRef `'realm-proposal'`, undoToken `null`) refuses while an advance is in flight or a paused interval is parked, then mints the order as a PENDING world-pulse proposal — the force-as-proposal lane: "Cancel = dismissWorldPulseProposal; approval = applyWorldPulseProposal (the realm-verb arm applies it force ≡ organic)" (campaignWorldPulseSlice.js:606-609). Recovery model, traced: PRE-apply, `dismissWorldPulseProposal` (campaignWorldPulseSlice.js:770; operationRegistry.js:105, receiptRef `'proposal-status'`, undoToken `null` — a dismissal cannot be un-refused, economy-family gap 11c); POST-apply, `applyWorldPulseProposal` (campaignWorldPulseSlice.js:586) ADVERTISES `undoToken:'undoLastPulse'` (operationRegistry.js:101) but is one of the four advertising rows that never arm the snapshot (VI.3 #41 / commands-surveyor gap 2), so an applied realm order's practical recovery is organic in-world resolution. All four verbs are lane-`'proposal'` ⇒ members of `executableRealmVerbs()` (realmManifest.js:493-495). All claims CONFIRMED by module + component + slice read this session.

## Addendum (brief-directed, OUT of population): the SED-04 lifecycle verbs

The brief asked to verify ransom / rescue / recall / return / stasis variants exist and record gating. **They exist, but NOT in the affordance manifest** — they are typed NPC pending-edit kinds riding the `queueEdit` → PendingChangesBar review → commit covenant (a parallel mutation lane to the composer):

- kinds: `ransom-npc`, `rescue-npc`, `recall-npc`, `return-npc`, `stasis-npc` — pendingEditIntents.js:72-77,109-114; pendingEdits.js:27,39-40,72
- stasis variants: exactly four typed reasons — `journey | imprisoned | missing | sequestered` (STASIS_REASONS, `src/domain/npc/npcOps.js`, validated at pendingEditIntents.js:586-588 → `stasis_reason_invalid`); labels in NpcLifecycleControls.jsx:43-48
- UI: NpcLifecycleControls.jsx — stasis/return via the Availability select (:97-105,168-190); ransom/rescue buttons appear ONLY while `npc.whereabouts.state === 'hostage'` (:110-114,194-233); recall ONLY while state is `traveling|visiting` and not hostage (:116-123,235-260)
- gating (all five): `canAuthorNpc` capability (fail-closed re-check inside the leaf, :83), desktop-only (`editingUnavailable = !canAuthorNpc || mobile || npcId == null`, :76 — mobile is read-mostly with a note, :262-269), durable NPC id required (legacy index-addressed NPCs are read-only, :270-277 — the SED-17 concern)
- timing per the intent table (pendingEditIntents.js:109-114): stasis/return = mechanical, **immediate** on commit (`npc.enter-stasis` / `npc.return-from-stasis`); ransom/rescue/recall = world-scope, **next-pulse** (`roads.ransom-hostage` / `roads.rescue-hostage` / `roads.recall` — "the simulation realizes the release on its next tick"; a recall "never teleports the NPC", :116-117)
- classification if they were rows: actionable (ransom/rescue/recall — party decisions resolved by the roads mover) and structural (stasis/return — typed status membership)
- status: CONFIRMED
- gap noted for the parent program: these five verbs and the 31 composer verbs are two disjoint mutation lanes (pendingEdits vs applyEvent) with separate review surfaces — the G-2b capability matrix (SED-04) must span both.

## Gaps

1. **dead-code / op-but-no-exposure — LINK_NEIGHBOUR is dormant.** The folded pseudo-verb (not in registry/manifest; delegates to `onLink`) only renders when an `onLink` handler is wired; the SOLE mount is `<EventComposer />` with no props (SettlementDetail.jsx:643), so the entry never appears anywhere. The composer's own comment says the feature "ships dormant until the fenced SettlementDetail.jsx passes it through" (EventComposer.jsx:60-63). CONFIRMED.
2. **no-recovery (draft lane).** Draft-phase applies mutate the settlement but write NO eventLog entry (settlementSlice.js:1754-1756), and `undoLastEvent` reads the log — so a draft apply has no undo. Draft is authorial (regen exists), but the same verbs advertise undo in canon. CONFIRMED.
3. **no-provenance (draft lane).** Same root: no timeline entry, no receipt trail for draft applies beyond the transient ActionResult. CONFIRMED.
4. **limited-recovery (canon).** The Timeline exposes undo for the LATEST entry only, and never while clock-bound (Timeline.jsx:70). Deeper entries are UI-irreversible even though undoEvent could compute them in reverse order. CONFIRMED.
5. **session-only batch cart.** The staged batch lives in component state (`staged`, EventComposer.jsx:133); navigating away or unmounting loses staged-but-unapplied work with no warning. CONFIRMED.
6. **dead-code — DEMOTE_NPC guard.** `canSubmit` still tests `type === 'DEMOTE_NPC'` (EventComposer.jsx:262) though DEMOTE can never be selected (folded, filtered from the list). Harmless, misleading. CONFIRMED.
7. **displayed-but-no-lever (UI-gate asymmetry) — SHARPER THAN RECORDED.** DESTROY_SETTLEMENT's type-the-name confirm is composer-UI-only; the store/command lane accepts the event without it (review is the implicit gate). Beyond that, `destroySavedSettlement` (settlementSlice.js:1184-1238) is a *separate registered canon operation* that destroys a save with no confirm, no manifest predicate, no pipeline, no veto channel, and no undo path. The invariant "one mutation path per verb" does not hold for this verb today. CONFIRMED. [corrected-by-verifier: the original entry framed this as a UI-vs-store asymmetry on ONE writer — evidence src/store/settlementSlice.js:1196-1213 and src/store/operationRegistry.js:61 show a second writer]
8. **doctrine note, not a conflict — KILL_NPC vs "never resolve a named character's fate."** The law binds the engine/AI; the DM verb is the deliberate legal lane, and the Surveyor path requires review. Record so a future autonomy wave doesn't wire canonEventApply to unreviewed KILL_NPC. CONFIRMED — but on **different evidence than first cited** [corrected-by-verifier-2: the original cite, canonEventApply.js:37, is the spec's `description` STRING ("Apply one reviewed canon event…"). The adapter enforces nothing about review: `validate()` checks only that `params.event` is a plain record with a string `type` (canonEventApply.js:43-49) and `preflight()` checks only that an `applyEvent` action and a `saveId` exist (:51-58). ## Addendum: OUT-OF-DENOMINATOR delegating composites [added-by-verifier]

Not members of the assigned population (they carry no `klass` and no exempt entry), and **correctly** so — the walker's own header documents them as CANNOT-CATCH #1: "a get()-DELEGATING orchestrator … references `get`, never `set`, so it is NOT in the denominator. Its effect is the sum of the registered sub-ops it invokes — covered transitively, not a new primitive verb. Such compositions are intentionally out of the registry" (tests/store/operationRegistry.walker.test.js:29-37, which names authSignOut / applyAllQueuedRegionalImpacts / setPrimaryDeity / imposeCult by name). Recorded here because a **capability atlas** is not a set()-census: these are real buttons a user presses, and no row in any K-A/B/C/D slice will ever describe them.

Live members touching this slice's neighbourhood (found by diffing every `^  name: (async )?(` property across `src/store/*Slice.js` against OPERATIONS ∪ EXEMPT_OPERATIONS):
- `discoverCampaignRegionalChannels` (campaignRegionalSlice.js:136-138) → `rebuildCampaignRegionalGraph(id, {discover:true})`. This is the ACTUAL name behind SettlementsPanel's "Discover channels"; the K-C rebuild row cites it but does not flag it as unregistered.
- `ignoreQueuedRegionalImpact` (campaignRegionalSlice.js:452-454) → `setRegionalImpactStatus(…, 'ignored')`. The Inbox's per-row Ignore button (RegionalImpactInbox.jsx:35,73) — the third terminal status alongside applied/resolved, and it is invisible to the K-C impact row.
- `applyAllQueuedRegionalImpacts` (campaignRegionalSlice.js:716-729) → sequential loop over `applyQueuedRegionalImpact`; `ignoreAllQueuedRegionalImpacts` (:731-740) → loop over `setRegionalImpactStatus`. Bulk verbs with no undo and no confirm.
- `setPrimaryDeity` / `imposeCult` (settlementSlice.js:2166-2167) → `*Impl(get, …)` in settlementDeityHelpers.js. Named in the walker's CANNOT-CATCH list; DEITY DOCTRINE surface.
- `authSignOut` (authSlice.js:455) → `get().clearAuth()`; `previewCampaignContentBindingMigration` / `…Rollback` (campaignSlice.js:626,635) and `importGalleryMap` (campaignSlice.js:664) are the same shape (the last is the map-only sibling of the registered map+campaign import).
- **[added-by-verifier-r2] `updateDossierNotes` (aiSlice.js:1042-1060), `pinNpc` (:1081-1092), `unpinNpc` (:1097-1109)** — the sharpest members of this class found in either pass, and the only ones that write DURABLE CLOUD state while staying out of the denominator. Each reads the save entry, rebuilds `aiData`, delegates the store write to `get().updateSavedSettlement(...)` (:1052, :1089, :1106) and then `await savesService.update(saveId, { aiData })` (:1054, :1090, :1107) — so the row is persisted to supabase, but the function itself never touches `set`, and the walker cannot see it. `pinNpc`/`unpinNpc` are load-bearing on determinism (the docstring at :1062-1074 states pinned NPCs ride every narrative request so they stay byte-identical across regenerations) and `updateDossierNotes.aiGuidance` is a direct input to `requestNarrative` (the K-C row's own `inputs` line cites aiSlice.js:353-355). Three real user verbs, one of them a determinism lever, none of them nameable by a future Surveyor that reads only the registry.

Disposition: NOT counted in the 117. Flagged as a **denominator-shape** finding — the registry is complete over set()-writers, not over user-facing verbs, and this atlas inherits that boundary.

## Gaps

1. **doctrine-conflict / no-recovery — uncanonize destroys the canon eventLog** with no snapshot and no receipt (settlementSlice.js:1425-1429). Immutable-evidence doctrine says history is annotatable, never rewritable; here it is silently wiped. CONFIRMED.
2. **no-recovery HAZARD — regenSection**: npcs branch durably destroys _userEdits/_authored (standing memory hazard); history branch is a documented deliberate deferral that destroys authored history + campaignEra entries (settlementSlice.js:1043-1062). CONFIRMED (code comment; hazard memory).
3. **unknown-reach/undo-drift — canonizeCampaignWorld's registry undoToken 'undoLastPulse'** is imprecise: the body pushes no pulseUndoStack snapshot, so the advertised undo only exists when an unrelated advance snapshot is on the session stack. **CONFIRMED** [corrected-by-verifier: mapper marked this PLAUSIBLE; the mechanism is now executed-evidence — `grep -n pulseUndoStack src/store/campaignAdvanceSession.js src/store/campaignWorldPulseDeferred.js src/store/campaignWorldPulseSlice.js` returns exactly one WRITE site that pushes (campaignAdvanceSession.js:406-412, inside `runAdvanceCampaignWorld` 175-571), one that pops (campaignWorldPulseDeferred.js:447,517), the declaration (slice :192) and the reader (slice :796). `runCanonizeCampaignWorld` (campaignWorldPulseDeferred.js:248-343 — signature re-read at :248 this pass) touches none of them] [corrected-by-verifier-r2: the round-1 evidence sentence OVER-NARROWS its own grep. `grep -rn pulseUndoStack src/store/` returns 13 lines across SIX files, not four sites: the three additional writers are `campaignSlice.js:144` (clears the stack outright), `campaignSlice.js:725` and `campaignDeletionSession.js:60` (both FILTER it, so a campaign delete/detach silently shortens the undo stack). The load-bearing conclusion is unchanged and stands — there is still exactly ONE site that PUSHES a snapshot — but the three extra mutators strengthen Gap 6 rather than this one: the lever can vanish mid-session from a campaign deletion, not only from a reload.]. The remaining PLAUSIBLE half is only the design intent — no test asserts the undoToken hint, so whether the registry entry is wrong or the body is missing a push is an owner call.
4. **no-provenance (durable) — the import family**: importGalleryMapWithCampaign, importGallerySettlement, importAccountData carry only GALLERY_IMPORTED analytics; no in-world/durable record of provenance survives on the imported entities. CONFIRMED.
5. **no-recovery — regional impact terminal statuses**: 'applied' blocks re-apply, 'resolved' blocks re-resolve, 'dismissed' proposals have no un-dismiss; advanceCampaignRegionalImpacts has no inverse. CONFIRMED (campaignRegionalSlice.js:487-740; campaignWorldPulseDeferred.js:787-789).
6. **displayed-but-no-lever (after reload) — pulse undo**: pulseHistory persists but pulseUndoStack is session-only, so the visible history outlives its undo lever (campaignWorldPulseSlice.js:190-192). Undone pulses also vanish from pulseHistory rather than being recorded as undone. CONFIRMED.
7. **dead-metadata — registry drift ×5** [corrected-by-verifier-r2: was ×3; two SHIPPED-COPY instances added as (d) and (e) below, and they are a different, worse severity than (a)-(c) — (a)-(c) are internal metadata, (d)-(e) are user-facing sentences]: (a) K-C section header says "(40)" vs 45 live macros (operationRegistry.js:62 — the exact rot class the K-B comment at :110-111 warns against); (b) hydrateServicesToggles attributed to configSlice but defined in toggleSlice.js:157 — the walker matches names only, so the `slice` field is unverified everywhere; (c) **the anti-rot comment's own prescribed command over-counts**: `grep -c "klass:'mechanical'"` returns 131 against 130 real mechanical entries, because the pattern matches the comment that recommends it (operationRegistry.js:111). **(d) [added-by-verifier-r2] `regenSection`'s registry DESCRIPTION is factually wrong about what the verb does**: it reads "Rebuilds one section of the settlement (**for example its power structure or economy**) …" (operationRegistry.js:64), but the body has exactly two branches — `if (section === 'npcs')` and `else if (section === 'history')` (settlementSlice.js:1039-1065), with no `else`. Power structure and economy are the two examples the verb CANNOT regenerate. **(e) [added-by-verifier-r2] `importNeighbour` / `handleImportDirect` descriptions claim the wrong destination**: "Imports another settlement as a neighbour **into the neighbour network**" (operationRegistry.js:92-93), but both write only `state.importedNeighbour`, the staging field for the NEXT generation (neighbourSlice.js:30-34, 79-82); `neighbourNetwork` is written exclusively by `addNeighbourLink`/`removeNeighbourLink`/`setNeighbourNetwork` (:46-69). **Why (d)-(e) are not cosmetic:** `description` is a REQUIRED, SHIPPED field, not a code comment — `scripts/generate-compendium-data.mjs:360-363` throws if any operation lacks one, and both wrong sentences are present verbatim in the committed `src/domain/compendium/generated/compendiumData.generated.js` (grepped byte-for-byte this pass), i.e. they are on the public Compendium surface the LEGIBILITY LAW governs, and `operationLabel()` (:380-382) is the accessor the future Surveyor reads. The cure for (a)-(c) is cheap and shared: derive the counts in the walker test (it already imports `OPERATIONS`) and assert the header numbers rather than transcribing or grepping them. (d)-(e) need a different cure — a copy pass over all 180 descriptions, since nothing in any gate checks a description against its verb's actual reach. CONFIRMED.
8. **no-provenance — silent bridge refusals**: undoCampaignStressorBridge's refusal paths (spread crisis, re-ignited twin) report only console.debug (campaignRegionalSlice.js:344,354,360); relationship-ripple edges carry no pointer back to their causing event. CONFIRMED.
9. **op-but-no-exposure — resolveCampaignStressor and the ripple pair** are bridge-only (no direct UI), which is fine, but they appear in the registry as first-class verbs the future Surveyor could name; the missing advance-guard on resolveCampaignStressor (unlike inject) would matter if ever exposed standalone. CONFIRMED asymmetry.
10. **influenceable-without-why guard rail (positive finding)**: no K-C macro writes a derived score directly — outlooks/systemState always re-derive (deriveSystemState calls at mutation sites). Determinism law holds across this population. CONFIRMED at the sites read.
11. **[added-by-verifier-r2] gating asymmetry across the four customContentSlice macros.** Three fence on the `canUseCustomContent()` premium/elevated predicate — `loadCustomContentFromCloud` (customContentSliceRuntime.js:664), `importCustomContentArchive` (customContentArchiveActions.js:83-89, which also refuses `ownerId === 'anon'`), `migrateLocalCustomContentToCloud` (:138-141) — while `applyCustomContentCommand`, the WRITE verb of the family, carries none: a `canUse|premium|tier|role` grep over its whole body (customContentSliceRuntime.js:199-365) returns zero hits and an anon caller lands on the local-ledger `ownerKey` branch. Not a vulnerability claim (the RPC is the authority and the UI gates the surface), but the atlas should not present the four as one gated family, and if the Surveyor ever names verbs from this registry the asymmetry becomes the difference between a refusal and a silent local write. A writer THROW is terminal `reconcile-required`, never plain failure ("retrying blindly would risk a duplicate", lines 248-257). ## SURVEYOR EXPOSURE RULESET
(for the assembly agent to normalize every other slice's `surveyor` column)

**The lawful loop, as BUILT today:** propose → review (per-item) → stage → approve → execute-as-command → receipt. Concretely:

1. **PROPOSE**: browser → edge function only (`src/lib/surveyorWrite.js` — "The browser NEVER calls a [provider]"; slug per stage, e.g. `interpret-session` at line 245). Credits estimated + charged at compile (interpret = 5 credits, `src/config/pricing.js:83`); refusals are typed (`classifyRefusal`, 402 = insufficient/nothing charged) and cordial-with-doors (§3d; `RefusalNote` renders refusalClass + doors).
2. **REVIEW**: per-item approve / edit / reject (`src/domain/intent/interpretReview.js` [corrected-by-verifier: was bare `interpretReview.js`, which in this ruleset's context reads as `src/lib/intent/` alongside `interpretApply.js` — no such file exists; the module is a DOMAIN module at `src/domain/intent/interpretReview.js`]); the PROTECTED-CONSENT BARRIER — an op carrying protectedFlags is INERT without an explicit `consented: true`; it lands in `blocked`, never silently dropped (`src/domain/intent/interpretReview.js:88-92`; UI tick `InterpretApplyPanel.jsx:173-186`). Undispatchable ops surface as `unroutable`, never swallowed (`InterpretApplyPanel.jsx:402-405`).
3. **STAGE**: the compile-time command target (owner/save/campaign + revisions) is CAPTURED at review start; navigating away or a revision change makes the command STALE rather than applying elsewhere (`InterpretApplyPanel.jsx:235-243`; executor identity+freshness checks).
4. **EXECUTE**: only through `executeSessionCommand` against `standardCommandRegistry` — never a direct writer call (boundary test pins the executor AND the panel).
5. **RECEIPT**: per-command receipt with transitions + persistence state; run-level reproducibility summary (engine version + seed + counts, content-free); ambiguous authoritative canon commands get a bounded same-session recovery action.

**What the loop may legally carry TODAY — exactly three command kinds** (`surveyorCapabilities()`, pinned twice):
- `settlement.canon-event.apply` (family canon_event → applyEvent)
- `campaign.party-impact.record` (family party_impact → recordPartyImpact)
- `content.definition.create-revision` (Surveyor Content studio approve flow, `source.type: 'surveyor'`)

**[corrected-by-verifier] HOW that three-kind ceiling is actually enforced — it is NOT a runtime gate.** `surveyorCapabilities()` has ZERO consumers in `src/`: `grep -rn surveyorCapabilities src/ tests/` returns the definition (`src/application/commands/commandRegistry.js:82-84`) and two TEST call sites (`tests/architecture/surveyorCommandBoundary.test.js:25`, `tests/application/commands/commandRegistry.test.js:50`) — nothing else. Likewise `spec.surveyor` is read at exactly one place, line 83 of that same filter. The executor never consults the flag: `executeCommand.js` dispatches on `registry.get(command.kind)` alone and would happily run any REGISTERED kind handed to it carrying `provenance: 'surveyor'`. The real ceiling is therefore three mechanisms, none of them the flag:
  1. the S3 dispatcher only maps two op families — `APPLY_FAMILIES = ['canon_event','party_impact']` (`src/domain/intent/applyDispatch.js:37`), so the interpret lane can mint only those two kinds;
  2. the Surveyor Content panel hard-codes `kind: 'content.definition.create-revision'` (`src/components/surveyor/CustomContentPanel.jsx:219` [corrected-by-verifier: prior pass cited `:218`, which is the `receipt = await applyCustomContentCommand({` line; the `kind:` literal is 219]);
  3. the two tests above, which fail if the declared flag set drifts.
  This does not weaken the doctrine — the boundary is real — but a normalizer must not describe `surveyor: true` as a permission the runtime checks. It is a DECLARATION policed by tests and shaped by the dispatcher. A new AI surface that built a registered non-Surveyor kind with `provenance: 'surveyor'` would execute, and only a human reading the boundary test would notice.

**Entitlement gate over ALL of it**: `isSurveyorTier` — surveyor entitlement OR founder OR admin/developer role; Cartographer premium NOT sufficient (`src/components/surveyor/surveyorGate.js:16-22` [corrected-by-verifier: path was unqualified; see the canon-event row]); fail-closed RPC fetch (`src/components/surveyor/useSurveyorEntitled.js:39-52`). **[added-by-verifier]** the predicate exists in TWO byte-identical copies by design — `src/components/account/useAccountSurveyorGate.js:22-26` [corrected-by-verifier: a prior pass cited `:16-19`, which is the explanatory comment block (16-21); the `export const surveyorEntitled = (auth) =>` predicate body runs 22-26] inlines it rather than importing, to avoid forming a shared chunk that would rebalance the first-paint closure (+42 B, measured — the comment states the number). A normalizer changing the gate must change both. **[added-by-verifier] and a guard already exists**: `tests/components/surveyorGateParity.test.js` is the divergence pin named in that comment — verified present on disk this pass. So this is a policed duplication, not an unguarded one.

**Normalization rules for other slices' `surveyor` columns:**
- A subject is `surveyor: stage` ONLY if its mutation flows through one of the three kinds above. Everything else is at most `explain`/`recommend` (read-model narration, musings register) or `none`.
- AI free text may land ONLY on presentation-effect/authored fields that pass the same admission walls as manual input (finite-semantics law); the create-revision lane satisfies this by construction (`admitCustomContentDefinitionShape` gates every entry).
- Derived/influenceable subjects must NEVER acquire a surveyor write path — the schema wall (no op type = no effect, §3 line 148-149) is the enforcement, and "the engine stays LLM-free" bars any per-tick AI.
- Never-resolve-a-named-fate: parley/persona surfaces are musings-register read-only; no command kind touches a named character's fate resolution.
- **CAVEAT for normalizers — FOUR Surveyor panels write OUTSIDE the command plane today** [corrected-by-verifier: was "two Surveyor panels"; a prior verifier pass censused all six `SurveyorWorkshop` stages (`SurveyorWorkshop.jsx:35-40` [corrected-by-verifier: prior pass wrote `:34-39`; line 34 is `const STAGES = [` and line 40 is the sixth stage]) for `useStore` writers and found two more. ### Structural NPC canon events
- members: ADD_NPC, KILL_NPC, ASSIGN_NPC_TO_ROLE, PROMOTE_NPC, DEMOTE_NPC (KILL_LEADER reuses KILL_NPC)
- class: actionable
- authority: event registry (src/domain/events/registry.js:224-290,773-800) + mutation handlers (src/domain/events/mutateEntities.js:400-560,753-830)
- operations: EventComposer builds the typed event (buildEvent.js:56-160; importance/role/institution/quality/swap-counterpart fields, EventComposer.jsx:118-149) → `applyEvent` (registered op, operationRegistry.js:57, eventLog receipt, undoToken undoLastEvent); Surveyor interpret-session can propose the same types via the canon_event family (applyDispatch.js:110-119)
- inputs: targetId (+ per-type payload: importance, role, institutionId, quality, cause, swapWithNpcId, ADD_NPC descriptive traits incl. secret/goal/temperament surfaced verbatim)
- preconditions: draft = authorial edit, canon = in-world event (registry comment :226-229); Surveyor path: IDENTITY_EVENT_TYPES (KILL_NPC/PROMOTE/DEMOTE/ASSIGN/KILL_LEADER) require explicit DM consent under canon + protected-target consent barrier for _authored entities (opVocabulary.js:26-29,77-88)
- timing: immediate on apply (+ propagation)
- scope: entity + linked institutions/factions (impairment propagation, mutateEntities.js:433-478)
- reach: ADD_NPC appends a `createNpc` row with `createdByEventId` (undo can drop it, mutateEntities.js:400-419); KILL_NPC sets `status:'dead'` + `removedByEventId` — the record is retained by *this mutation* (entities/npcs.js:150-151) — and lands importance-scaled staffing/leadership impairments with the re-assert-after-propagation correction (mutateEntities.js:425-478); stateDeltas (resilience/volatility) per registry. [corrected-by-verifier: was "the record is RETAINED, never deleted" — REFUTED for the party-caused path. When the composer's "party caused" toggle is on (EventComposer.jsx:114,703-711 → `partyCaused: true`), `mapEventToPartyImpact` (partyEventLinkage.js:31-37,61-77) converts KILL_NPC **and** KILL_LEADER into a `remove_npc` party-impact action, dispatched from settlementSlice.js:271 and drainQueuedEvents.js:164; the pulse handler then DROPS the roster row outright — `npcs: settlement.npcs.filter((_n, i) => i !== idx)` (partyImpact.js:376-379) — with the header comment stating the intent: "drop the named NPC from the settlement's roster so the dossier stops listing a corpse" (partyImpact.js:356-361). So a party-caused kill deletes the person; only a non-party-caused kill leaves the `status:'dead'` tombstone.]
- preview: deterministic-scope — `previewEvent` is pure, preview≡apply, staleness-keyed (settlementSlice.js previewEvent + Composer V2 §5 staleness law)
- [added-by-verifier-2] **ADD_NPC is not the only creation path in this cluster.** `assignNpcMutation` opens with `findNpc(s, event.targetId) || createNpc({ name: labelFromTarget(event.targetId) })` (mutateEntities.js:481) and then replace-or-INSERTS (:502-504); the manifest predicate is deliberately open — `predicate: () => ok(), // creates the NPC when missing — never gated` (affordanceManifest.js:402). So ASSIGN_NPC_TO_ROLE against an unrecognised name silently mints a person with no `createdByEventId` stamp, which means `inferSource` tags them 'generated' rather than 'event' (canonStatus.js:104) and a later `regenSection('npcs')` will roll them away — unlike an ADD_NPC creation, which is protected (canonStatus.js:104 reads `createdByEventId`). Verified by reading both handlers; the asymmetry is real and undocumented.
- persistence: eventLog + settlement in the save blob (applyEvent persist triple)
- recovery: `undoLastEvent` (most recent only, operationRegistry.js:58)
- provenance: eventLog entry per event (receiptRef 'eventLog-entry')
- exposure: EventComposer / Timeline on SettlementDetail; Surveyor review flow — but NOT uniformly across the five members [corrected-by-verifier: was a flat "EventComposer / Timeline". `authorableVerbs()` (affordanceManifest.js:685-688) filters out every manifest entry carrying `foldedInto`, and both **DEMOTE_NPC** (affordanceManifest.js:600-602, folded into PROMOTE_NPC: "a promote of A is a demote of B") and **KILL_LEADER** (:587, folded into KILL_NPC) carry it — neither appears in the composer's verb rail or the ComposerNavigator search. They remain registry-real and Surveyor-proposable (IDENTITY_EVENT_TYPES includes KILL_LEADER, opVocabulary.js:26-29), but they are op-but-no-composer-lever. Composer-exposed members are ADD_NPC (free identity, `entityKind:'settlement'`, affordanceManifest.js:389-393), KILL_NPC (targetsFrom 'npcs', :394-398), ASSIGN_NPC_TO_ROLE (targetsFrom 'npcs', :399-403) and PROMOTE_NPC (custom swap picker, `entityKind:'npcs'`, :404-409).]
- destination: legacy-retained — the composer is a working typed-order surface; G-4 verb work may re-skin, not replace

### NPC succession / replacement (successorNpc) [added-by-verifier-2]
- members: `successorNpc(ousted, rng)` (a whole new NPC), `replaceOustedNpcs(settlement, oustedNames, rng)` (the roster swap)
- class: actionable on the event path, influenceable on the pulse path — a single mechanism with two triggers
- authority: `settlement.npcs[i]` REPLACED wholesale by a generated stranger; src/domain/worldPulse/successorNpc.js:28-54 (mint) and :58-80 (`replaceOustedNpcs`)
- operations (both triggers verified): (a) **EXPOSE_CORRUPTION against a corrupt NPC** — `exposeCorruption` dispatches to `exposeCorruptNpc` (mutateEntities.js:593), which maps the roster through `successorNpc` (mutateEntities.js:656). Reachable from the EventComposer (Power family), the Session Ledger (`exposure` effect, TableLedgerPanel.jsx:212), and the Surveyor (canon_event family). (b) **organic ousting in the world pulse** — `replaceOustedNpcs` imported by pulseKernel.js:46, fired for NPCs the corruption layer ousts on a tick
- inputs: the ousted NPC (seat fields are copied forward) + a seeded PRNG (`createPRNG('successor:<eventId>:<name>')`, mutateEntities.js:655 — deterministic per event)
- preconditions: (a) the target must already be `corrupt`; (b) engine-internal
- timing: immediate on apply (event path) / next-pulse (organic path); scope: entity (+ the tied criminal and home institutions via `applyCorruptionImpairments`)
- reach: the successor INHERITS seat + standing — role, category, factionAffiliation, factionLink, institutionId, importance, power, influence, and `personality.modifier/tell/speech` — but gets a NEW `id`, a NEW `name`, a re-rolled `personality.dominant`/`flaw`, `goal.short = SUCCESSOR_GOAL`, `corrupt:false`, `timesExposed:0`, and `replacedNpc:<old name>`. Because the id changes, every id-keyed reference to the departed person breaks: `settlement.relationships` edges (npc1Id/npc2Id), the AI pin key (`aiData.pinnedNpcs` holds the old id), `npcStates` sidecar entries, and any `_userEdits` the DM had authored on that NPC. Nothing re-projects them — `refreshRelationshipProjections` runs ONLY inside `regenNPCsPipeline` (generateSettlementPipeline.js:327-328), never on this path
- preview: deterministic-scope on the event path (`previewEvent` is pure and the successor PRNG is event-id-seeded, so preview ≡ apply); none on the pulse path
- persistence: eventLog + save blob (event path) / campaign state via advance commit (pulse path)
- recovery: `undoLastEvent` on the event path only — and it restores the settlement blob, so it does bring the person back. The pulse path has no compensating verb
- provenance: `replacedNpc` on the successor is the ONLY on-entity trace; the departed NPC leaves no tombstone row and no `removedByEventId` (unlike KILL_NPC)
- exposure: no dedicated control — it is the invisible tail of a verb the DM chose for a different reason ("expose the corrupt magistrate"), which is exactly why it was missed twice
- destination: needs an owner ruling — same class as `remove_npc` (Gap 13). At minimum the composer's EXPOSE_CORRUPTION copy should say that the exposed NPC is replaced, not merely scarred
- surveyor: **stage** — EXPOSE_CORRUPTION is a registered EVENT_TYPE so it rides `canonEventTypes`, and it is NOT in IDENTITY_EVENT_TYPES, so an AI-proposed exposure of a named character never hits the CANON_IDENTITY consent barrier
- maturity: built
- status: CONFIRMED (dispatch, handler, mint, and both call sites read end-to-end)
- evidence: mutateEntities.js:586-664 (dispatch :593, header :637-639, substitution :655-656); successorNpc.js:28-54,58-80; pulseKernel.js:46; TableLedgerPanel.jsx:212; opVocabulary.js:26-29
- notes/gaps: MISSED BY BOTH THE MAPPER AND THE FIRST VERIFIER. The mapper filed successorNpc twice as background machinery ("the vacated seat refills via existing role-fill machinery", seat-reassignment row) without ever noticing it MINTS AND SWAPS a person; the first verifier cited successorNpc.js:51 for `replacedNpc` and still did not disposition the operation that writes it.

4. **op-but-no-exposure — instantNpc**: complete seeded generator, zero importers. CONFIRMED (dead-code-until-wired).
5. **Pin/lock do NOT protect through reroll (doctrine-conflict / stale-doc)**: regen preservation and Surveyor protected-context read `entity.pinned`/`entity.locked`, but pins live in `aiData.pinnedNpcs` and locks in `state.locks` — nothing in src/ ever stamps either flag on an NPC entity (greps: no writer of `npc.pinned` or entity `.locked = true`). Consequences: (a) a pinned-but-unedited NPC is rerolled by regenSection despite aiSlice.js:1076 saying "so regenerations don't rewrite it"; (b) pinned NPCs are absent from the Surveyor consent barrier (opVocabulary.js:52-54 checks a flag that never exists); (c) `setLock` remains inert for regen (memory's claim still true post-fix). Cure shape: stamp/read a join at the preservation + protected-context seams, or scope the aiSlice docstring. CONFIRMED.
6. **Registered-but-unexposed editable paths**: EDITABLE_FIELDS npc `goal.short`/`personality`/`role` have no editor; `goal.short` additionally has a two-writer seam (free-prose registry vs bank-facet sync). CONFIRMED.
7. **No pre-regen snapshot (no-recovery)**: commitPendingEdits snapshots before writing; regenSection('npcs') persists durably with no snapshot — the unauthored cast is unrecoverable by design, but the asymmetry with the queue spine is unrecorded. CONFIRMED.
8. **Doc drift — pendingEdits.js:67-69** claims each NPC op has "a registered operation (operationRegistry)"; none has a dedicated entry (they ride queueEdit/commitPendingEdits). **npcOps.js:5-6** claims the store dispatchers call its pure bodies; applyNpcOp re-implements them inline (imports only validateNpcFacet) and skips the `reassignedTo` provenance stamp the pure body writes. PLAUSIBLE (matches the recorded T4 gap; not exhaustively traced this session).

12. **Deliberate deferrals (documented, not bugs)**: history regen destroys authored history (settlementSlice.js:1043-1062, owner decision); mobile NPC editing read-mostly (NpcLifecycleControls.jsx:87-90,262-268); alignment/role facet sim-adoption seam owner-gated (npcOps.js:16-21).

This is the sharpest tension in the family with "never resolve a named character's fate" and with the stasis row's "a shelf, not a grave". CONFIRMED. Owner ruling wanted.
14. **[added-by-verifier] Surveyor consent-barrier hole for the corruption + party verbs.** `IDENTITY_EVENT_TYPES` (opVocabulary.js:26-29) covers KILL_NPC / PROMOTE_NPC / DEMOTE_NPC / ASSIGN_NPC_TO_ROLE / KILL_LEADER. It does NOT cover **IMPOSE_CORRUPTION** (which covertly turns a named NPC) or the **party-impact kinds** (which are a separate vocabulary arm entirely, `buildOpVocabulary` :38-43, and never pass through IDENTITY_EVENT_TYPES at all). A Surveyor-proposed corruption or removal therefore reaches review without the identity-consent gate. CONFIRMED.
15. **[added-by-verifier] `npc.tags` is a dead read arm — upgrade from UNDISPOSITIONED to CONFIRMED.** THE FACET LAW's declared side accepts either `npc.facets.<kind>` or a `facet:<kind>:<value>` tag (npcBank.js:11-13 → `facetOf` in spatial/cohesionWeave.js). Grepping every `.tags` write across src/domain/npc, src/generators/npcGenerator.js and src/domain/worldPulse returns only institution specs, news-entry tags and entrepot goods — **no code path ever writes a tag onto an NPC**. The tag arm of the facet law is unreachable for NPCs today; only the `facets` object arm is live. CONFIRMED (writer-absence grep, three roots).
16. **[added-by-verifier] `setLock` registry description drifts the same way the pin docstring does.** operationRegistry.js:128 describes setLock as "Locks a section of the settlement **so it is preserved when other sections regenerate**". `state.locks` is a flat key map (settlementSlice.js:1532-1538) that neither `regenSection` nor `mergePreservedNpcs`/`preservesEntity` ever reads. Same shape as Gap 5, but on a second surface, and this one is walked into the shipped compendium. CONFIRMED.

17. **[added-by-verifier-2] doctrine-conflict / no-tombstone — EXPOSE_CORRUPTION deletes the named character it exposes.** `exposeCorruption` → `exposeCorruptNpc` → `successorNpc` substitution (mutateEntities.js:593, 656). This is more exposed than Gap 13's `remove_npc`, on three counts: it is reachable from THREE live surfaces (EventComposer, Session Ledger, Surveyor) rather than one; the DM chose the verb for a different stated purpose ("expose the corrupt magistrate"), so the deletion is a hidden tail; and the composer/ledger copy nowhere says the person is replaced. It also silently orphans every id-keyed reference to the departed NPC (relationship edges, `aiData.pinnedNpcs`, `npcStates`, `_userEdits`) because the successor takes a NEW id, and nothing re-projects. Mitigations that DO exist: `undoLastEvent` restores the blob on the event path, and the successor PRNG is event-id-seeded so preview ≡ apply. CONFIRMED. Owner ruling wanted — at minimum honest copy on the verb; ideally the tombstone-or-successor choice becomes a dial.
18. **[added-by-verifier-2] The identity-consent barrier misses the two verbs that actually remove people.** `IDENTITY_EVENT_TYPES` (opVocabulary.js:26-29) gates KILL_NPC / PROMOTE / DEMOTE / ASSIGN / KILL_LEADER — of which only KILL_NPC removes anyone, and it leaves a `status:'dead'` tombstone. The two verbs that genuinely delete a roster row — **EXPOSE_CORRUPTION** (Gap 17) and **remove_npc** (Gap 13) — are both outside it. Gap 14 named the corruption hole for IMPOSE_CORRUPTION; verifier-2 upgrades it: the same hole is worse for EXPOSE_CORRUPTION, because IMPOSE only flips a flag while EXPOSE removes the person. CONFIRMED.
19. **[added-by-verifier-2] Citation drift in the mapper's regen/preservation block (documentation defect, not a behaviour defect).** Five citations in the headline paragraph and the reroll/relationships rows point 60-80 lines off (see the inline corrections). Cause is visible in `git status`: `src/domain/regenerationPreservation.js` is UNTRACKED and `generateSettlementPipeline.js` is MODIFIED — this is live parallel work whose line numbers move under a reader. Anyone quoting this slice against those two files must re-resolve first. CONFIRMED.

### Gaps added by the verifier

10. **contract-violated-in-code (conversion patron embed drops `lawAxis`)** — **CONFIRMED, NEW.** `reEmbedPrimaryDeity` (src/domain/worldPulse/applyWorldPulse.js:574-588) documents itself as re-picking "the exact embed field set (mirrors mutate.setPrimaryDeity)" but omits `lawAxis`, which setPrimaryDeity writes with an explicit `|| 'neutral'` default and an in-code note that the default exists for byte-identity on that axis (mutateEntities.js:855-857). An organically converted patron therefore carries no law axis while a DM-assigned one always does. This is a determinism/parity defect on a lifecycle path (pulse conversion) that the atlas's patron row treated as covered by the DM path.
11. **no-recovery on a non-DM write path (patron replacement by conversion)** — **CONFIRMED, NEW.** The pulse conversion replaces `config.primaryDeityRef` + `primaryDeitySnapshot` with no canon event, so there is no event-log entry, no `undoToken`, and no `faithEventFilter` gating of the resulting name change. The undo guarantee documented at undoEvent.js:86-91 covers SET_PRIMARY_DEITY only.
12. **ref-namespace leak (`converted:` refs)** — **CONFIRMED, NEW.** applyWorldPulse.js:578 can mint `converted:<stablePart>` as a deity ref when the incoming snapshot carries no `_deityRef`. That namespace is recognized by neither the account mint (`deity:<scope>:<slug>`, settlementDeityHelpers.js:27-34) nor the pool namespace (`deity:core:`, deityPool.js:57-62), yet the pantheon ledger keys by deity id (pantheon.js:7). Relevant to the owner-gated deity:core: lifecycle trace: a removal sweep that greps only `deity:core:` and `custom:` will miss this third namespace.
13. **missing verb rows (EXPOSE_CORRUPTION; PROMOTE_NPC / DEMOTE_NPC)** — **CONFIRMED absence in the original map.** EXPOSE_CORRUPTION is now rowed above. ## Verification

**Verifier:** adversarial pass, 2026-07-26, against the same live tree (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` → `claude/composite-r4`, re-confirmed at session start). Repo treated as read-only; the only file written is this one.

**Method.** For each sampled row I (a) opened the cited file at the cited lines and checked the evidence line actually says what is claimed; (b) attacked the row's *authority* claim with an exhaustive assignment-site grep rather than accepting the cited writer; (c) attacked the row's *exposure* claim by reading the mounting component, not the manifest; (d) re-enumerated the population by content grep with different terms from the mapper's filename `find`.

**Sampling.** 21 of the original 24 rows independently re-derived (all four pillars; every interaction class present — authorable, structural, actionable, influenceable, presentational, inspect-only, mixed). Not re-derived: *Faction structural metrics*, *Faction relationship web*, *Custom deity definitions* — sampled only through their shared citations (userEdits.js, rulingStructure.js, customContentSchema line ranges), so their status lines are inherited, not verified. Treat those three as unverified rather than confirmed.

**Counts.**
- Rows checked: **21**
- Rows fully confirmed as written: **12** (faction rename; faction existence *mechanics*; governing seat/CHANGE_RULING_POWER; public legitimacy; stability + recent conflict; criminal capture; intra-faction ladder; current tensions; power strata + support web; cult imposition *mechanics*; faith surface gating; deity effect preview)
- Rows with at least one refuted or materially corrected claim: **9** (faction description — status upgraded; faction existence — inputs/exposure; faction impairment — authority; patron deity assignment — authority + recovery + two new defects; cult imposition — evidence citation; latent pantheon — activation authority + strip site upgraded; faith profile — object shape; divine mandate — wrong function and wrong location; realm pantheon ledger — write-side no longer unverified)
- Status downgrades: **1** (patron deity assignment, CONFIRMED → CONFIRMED-for-DM-path / REFUTED as single-writer)
- Status upgrades earned by verification: **3** (faction desc app-wide exposure PLAUSIBLE → CONFIRMED; latent-pantheon strip site hedge → CONFIRMED; realm pantheon materialization PLAUSIBLE → CONFIRMED)
- New rows added: **2** (EXPOSE_CORRUPTION; faction blocs / settlementPolitics)
- New gaps added: **6** (items 10-15)
- Denominator: mapper ≈60 by filename → verifier **132** by content; **15 silent drops** and **4 misfilings** listed above

**Verdict.** The slice's *mechanism* descriptions are strong — where the mapper read a handler, it read it correctly, and its quoted in-code laws are faithful. The failure mode is systematically at the *edges*: it equates "the DM lever's handler" with "the field's authority" (patron deity, faction impairment), it trusts the manifest over the mounted component (ADD_FACTION), and its filename-based denominator could not see the pulse subsystems that write the very fields it rows. The two new defects (dropped `lawAxis` on conversion re-embed; the `converted:` ref namespace) are the substantive product of this pass and are worth carrying into the owner-gated deity:core: lifecycle trace.

**Verdict (pass 2).** The atlas is now substantially trustworthy on mechanism and materially improved at the edges, but two systemic lessons should travel with it rather than stay buried in this slice. First, **a capability atlas must prove reachability from the OPERATION's caller census, not from the presence of a UI primitive** — that single method error produced both a wrong proof in pass 1 and, once corrected, the largest finding in the slice (24 of 25 authored-prose capabilities are phantom). Second, **no single enumeration axis is adequate for this population**: filename, state key, and import edge each found members the other two structurally could not see, so every slice should record which axis it used and treat "nothing dropped" as unprovable from one. ### [added-by-verifier] Simulation Rules — the economy governors
- class: structural (user-owned campaign policy; decides whether the engine may author economy at all)
- authority: `campaign.worldState.simulationRules` — defaults `src/domain/worldPulse/simulationRules.js` :36-52; normalizer `normalizeSimulationRules`; presets `SIMULATION_RULE_PRESETS` (four grid presets, SimulationRulesDialog :72-78)
- operations: per-subsystem toggles rendered from `TOGGLES` (SimulationRulesDialog.jsx :56-65) — the economy-relevant ones are `resourceDriftEnabled` ("Resources"), `tierDriftEnabled` ("Promotion/demotion"), `institutionLifecycleEnabled` ("Institution lifecycle"), plus `tradeFlowsEnabled` / `migrationFlowsEnabled` in the tri-state domain rows; the "Who decides" axis carries `majorChangesRequireProposal`; `intensity` (conservative/normal/dramatic, :40-44) scales every probability band
- inputs: booleans, tri-states, an intensity enum, a preset pick
- preconditions: a campaign (these are campaign-scoped, not save-scoped)
- timing: takes effect at the next advance
- scope: **campaign** — a scope no other row in this slice has (settlement, config-global, or cross-save)
- reach: gates `institutionLifecycle`, resource drift, tier drift, trade flows; `majorChangesRequireProposal` decides whether a founding/dissolution/depletion/tier-crossing auto-applies or becomes a DM proposal (`changeAuthorityPolicy.js` :96-127; `resource_depletion`, `tier_change`, `institution_lifecycle` are all `authority: 'proposal-gated', consultsProposalFlag: true`). `DEFAULT_SIMULATION_RULES` ships every economy flag TRUE and `majorChangesRequireProposal` TRUE (:45-52), so the shipped default is "the engine proposes, the DM disposes"
- preview: none; `pulseFingerprint.js` :253 folds these keys into the determinism fingerprint, so changing one is a declared change of world behaviour
- persistence: campaign worldState
- recovery: flip back / re-pick a preset; no per-change undo
- provenance: `presetId` + `schemaVersion` on the rules object; no edit trail
- exposure: `src/components/map/SimulationRulesDialog.jsx` (+ `SimulationRulesAxes.jsx`), reached from the world map / realm toolbar
- destination: dock (a campaign-policy surface, not a settlement one)
- surveyor: none
- maturity: built
- status: CONFIRMED
- evidence: simulationRules.js:36-52,279, SimulationRulesDialog.jsx:40-78, changeAuthorityPolicy.js:96-127, pulseFingerprint.js:253
- notes/gaps: this is the single largest lever over whether the economy rows above ever change on their own, and it lives on the map, three surfaces away from every dossier economy tab. Nothing in EconomicsTab/ServicesTab/ResourcesTab tells a DM that "Institution lifecycle" is on.

### [added-by-verifier] World-pulse proposal adjudication (approve / dismiss engine-authored economy changes)
- class: actionable (a real two-verb decision surface over economy-family structural changes)
- authority: campaign pulse record + proposal status — `src/store/campaignWorldPulseSlice.js` `applyWorldPulseProposal` :586, `dismissWorldPulseProposal` :770, `undoLastPulse` :808
- operations: `applyWorldPulseProposal` (operationRegistry :101 — `klass:'macro'`, `receiptRef:'pulse-record'`, `undoToken:'undoLastPulse'`) and `dismissWorldPulseProposal` (:105 — `receiptRef:'proposal-status'`, `undoToken:null`)
- inputs: `(campaignId, proposalId)` — approve or reject a single proposal
- preconditions: a pending proposal, which only exists because `majorChangesRequireProposal` is on for the kinds `changeAuthorityPolicy` marks proposal-gated
- timing: immediate on approve (the change commits to campaign canon)
- scope: campaign → the named settlement
- reach: the economy-family proposal kinds are `institution_lifecycle` (a founding or dissolution), `resource_depletion`, `tier_drift_collapse` / `tier_change` (which restructure the whole economic profile) — i.e. this desk is where a DM accepts or refuses an institution closing and a resource running out
- preview: the proposal carries its headline + rationale before commit
- persistence: campaign worldState + pulse record
- recovery: **asymmetric** — approve is undoable via `undoLastPulse`; dismiss records a status with `undoToken:null` and no way back
- provenance: pulse-record receipt on approve; proposal-status receipt on dismiss
- exposure: `src/components/map/WorldPulsePanel.jsx` :32-33 and `src/components/map/HeraldAdjudication.jsx` :232, :305-306 (the Herald's Adjudication desk)
- destination: dock (session/realm ledger) — this is already the Adjudication desk the table-event row points at
- surveyor: none for adjudication itself
- maturity: built
- status: CONFIRMED
- evidence: operationRegistry.js:101,105,108, campaignWorldPulseSlice.js:586,770,808, WorldPulsePanel.jsx:32-33, HeraldAdjudication.jsx:232,305-306, changeAuthorityPolicy.js:96-127
