## Gaps

1. **displayed-implies-consequence / unknown-reach inverse — Network effects are display-only.** `getSettlementModifiers`/`getAllModifiers` totals are consumed by exactly four display surfaces (panel, echo, list badge, PDFs) and nothing in the engine. The panel presents them as "cascading modifiers" acting on the settlement; no generator, pulse, or event handler reads them. Either wire them as a declared input (owner-gated — would shift goldens) or label the panel as advisory. CONFIRMED (consumer grep this session). relationshipGraph.js:372, SettlementDetailNetworkEffectsPanel.jsx:10.
2. **Stale-derivation window (timing gap).** `applyEvent` mutates institutions/resources/config but `reconcileSettlementChange` does not re-run the economy pass (settlementReconciliation.js:30-63) — `availableServices`, `activeChains`, prosperity, `resourceAnalysis` keep their generation-time values until the next full regeneration/pulse rebuild. ADD_INSTITUTION shows the institution but not its services/chains; the tabs partially compensate with live overlays (computeChainSets). CONFIRMED for the reconcile step; the absence of ANY other post-event rebuild seam is PLAUSIBLE (not exhaustively proven). **[amended-by-critic-pass: the field-level substrate that DECLARES which economy fields must stay live vs stay honestly frozen EXISTS — `src/domain/fieldManifest.js` `FROZEN_VS_LIVE` pins `economicState.foodSecurity.{storageMonths,resilienceScore,deficitPct,surplusPct}` as mode `'live'` with named pulse writers, and `foodSecurity.{dailyNeed,dailyProduction}` / `magicTradeChannel` as mode `'snapshot'` with explicit displayRules, enforced by `tests/joins/fieldManifest.test.js`. The stale window described here for `activeChains`/`availableServices`/prosperity is exactly the bug class that manifest was built to pin, and NONE of those three fields is listed in it yet (its stated HONEST LIMIT: "new, unlisted fields cannot be auto-detected"). See the Part IV substrate rows and §2.]**
3. **no-recovery + no-provenance — neighbour link membership.** Dossier `removeNeighbour` (SettlementDetail.jsx:704) and `neighbourSlice.addNeighbourLink/removeNeighbourLink` mutate the same `neighbourNetwork` array the relationship EVENTS carefully snapshot for undo, but as plain store writes: no eventLog entry, no undo, analytics-only provenance. CONFIRMED.
4. **no-provenance — draft-phase events.** By design, draft applies produce the same state delta but no timeline entry (settlementSlice:1750-1756 [corrected-by-verifier: was :1735-1737]). Recorded here as a deliberate posture, not a bug — but it means a draft-mode IMPAIR leaves only `causeEventId` stamps as archaeology.
5. **op-but-no-exposure (partial) — table-event lane excludes economy verbs.** The session-ledger/table lane can author stressors and corruption exposure but no institution/resource/trade-good verbs (settlementPendingEditWriters.js:14-18). If the Adjudication desk is meant to cover "what happened at the table," a burned granary cannot currently be recorded through it — only via the composer. CONFIRMED as-coded; whether it is a gap is an owner call.

CONFIRMED by independent read (ServicesTab.jsx holds only local `search`/`openCats` UI state and no store writer; ResourcesTab.jsx has no `onClick` and no store import at all). Configuring institutions/services/goods for one settlement silently shapes the next generation, with bulk reset as the only recovery. Same class as Gap 3, one order of magnitude wider. 10. **[added-by-verifier] promise/behaviour mismatch — authored institution prose does not survive regeneration.** `userEdits.js` sets `_authored: true`, which `canonStatus.js` promotes to `source:'user'`, `canonStatus:'canon'`, `locked:true` — but the module's own header (:36-40) records that only the NPC reroll has a preservation tail, so an edited institution description is replaced wholesale by its regenerate path. Instance of the known regen-edit-loss class, landing on an economy-family entity. 11a. **[added-by-verifier, 2nd pass] dead branch behind a live handler — a DM IMPAIR can never break a food anchor.** `mutateEntities.js:258-260` gates the `food_anchor_lost` rise on `severity >= 0.6 && type === 'capacity'`, but `EventComposer.jsx:129-132` hard-codes `dimension = 'legitimacy'` for every IMPAIR_INSTITUTION (severity 0.7), deliberately hiding both from the DM. So the branch is reachable only from REMOVE_INSTITUTION (which hard-codes 0.7 capacity) and the folded, unauthorable DAMAGE_INSTITUTION. Either the composer needs a dimension choice ("close the mill" vs "disgrace the mill") or the capacity branch should be documented as remove-only. CONFIRMED by reading both sides. This is also a legibility gap in the opposite direction from Gap 7: the verb's LABEL ("Impair institution") promises a general weakening; the code delivers exactly one axis.

11b. **[added-by-verifier, 2nd pass] two provenance ledgers and two undo tokens over one roster.** The composer's institution/resource verbs stamp `createdByEventId` / `causeEventId` / eventLog and are reversed by `undoLastEvent`; the world pulse's institution and resource writes stamp `createdByWorldPulseOutcomeId` / `_worldPulseFounded` / `institutionHistory` / `resourceHistory` and are reversed only by `undoLastPulse`. Neither undo can see the other's records, and both write the SAME `settlement.institutions` array and the SAME `config.resourceEdits` record. Nothing in the dossier distinguishes a DM-built smithy from an engine-built one. CONFIRMED by reading both writer sets and both scrub paths. Whether the two ledgers should merge is an owner call; that they are currently invisible to each other is not.

11c. **[added-by-verifier, 2nd pass] asymmetric recovery on the proposal desk.** `applyWorldPulseProposal` carries `undoToken:'undoLastPulse'`; `dismissWorldPulseProposal` carries `undoToken:null` (operationRegistry.js:101,105). A DM who refuses an engine-proposed institution closure cannot un-refuse it. CONFIRMED as-coded; same class as Gap 3, on a campaign-scoped surface.

12. **[added-by-verifier] scope-creep risk — prosperity has engine writers the atlas said it had none of.** Four pulse/roads movers step `economicState.prosperity` (see the prosperity row). Any future "prosperity is generation-only, safe to cache" reasoning built on the mapper's original wording would be wrong. CONFIRMED by grep on the spread-write form.

## SECTION 4 — The AI lane (finite-semantics enforcement)

### Surveyor custom-content authoring
- class: authorable (same subject as Section 2; this row maps the AI path)
- authority: shared workflow state machine `contentDraftSession.js` (pure reducer; stages describe→inspect→effects→sample→revise→approve→receipt, contentDraftSession.js:16-24); Surveyor UI src/components/surveyor/CustomContentPanel.jsx
- operations: `compileCustomContent` posts intent + `{manifestVersion}` handshake to edge write slug `custom-content` (src/lib/surveyorWrite.js:137-152); returns `draft = {entries, unsupported}` — the AI is a **bucketing clerk**: it may only propose entries in authorable buckets with manifest fields; anything unmappable lands in the `unsupported` array, counted against `mappingRate` (contentEffectProjection.js:216-231)
- preconditions/walls (in order): edge validation is declared "necessary but not sufficient" — approval re-validates the COMPLETE base definition (and edit-approval the complete merged definition) against the same generated client manifest (contentReview.js:1-11); deterministic effect interpretation is derived LOCALLY, never trusted from the model ("AI may propose a structure, but it never explains its own authority", contentEffectProjection.js:5-8); per-entry decisions approve/edit/reject/pending (CONTENT_REVIEW_ACTIONS, contentReview.js:13-18); any decision change invalidates interpretation AND sample together (contentDraftSession.js:247-262); a baseline (environment) change mid-flow forces a fresh same-seed sample (contentDraftSession.js:265-287); approval completes ONLY on a confirmed durable receipt — ambiguous truthy responses are coerced to `reconcile-required`/`unconfirmed` (contentDraftSession.js:107-148); the write goes through the identical `applyCustomContentCommand` with `source: {type:'surveyor', ref: requestId}` (CustomContentPanel.jsx:216-229)
- timing: staged, multi-gate · preview: exact + deterministic-scope (same seed constant as manual lane, CustomContentPanel.jsx:165)
- provenance: source type `surveyor` + request id recorded in the command
- exposure: Surveyor Workshop → CustomContentPanel; manual editor shares the same rails (CustomContent.jsx:117-118 "Manual authoring uses the same deterministic interpretation/sample rails as the Surveyor lane")
- surveyor: stage — this IS the staging implementation; nothing auto-applies
- doctrine verdict: finite-semantics law CONFIRMED structurally — free text can only land on P-fields; mechanical fields are enum/boolean/reference and pass the same admission wall regardless of author (human or AI)
- maturity: built (uncommitted) · status: CONFIRMED
- evidence: contentDraftSession.js:1-426 (read in full), contentReview.js:1-40, CustomContentPanel.jsx:111-230, surveyorWrite.js:137-152, contentEffectProjection.js:1-232 (read in full)
- [corrected-by-verifier] SECOND CALLER OF THE SAME AI SLUG — the row's claim that "the write goes through the identical `applyCustomContentCommand`" is true of `CustomContentPanel.jsx` ONLY. `src/components/surveyor/CorpusFactoryPanel.jsx:82-92` is a second consumer of `compileCustomContent` and of the metered `getSurveyorAiCost('customContent')` budget (:72): it takes `res.draft.entries` and maps each into a **staged corpus candidate** via `stageCorpusCandidates(...)`, bypassing admission, the taste gate, and the command boundary entirely. This is doctrine-clean — nothing there writes custom content or canon ("Nothing here writes canon: the owner's taste is the gate", CorpusFactoryPanel.jsx:1-10); approved candidates only render a build-time `APPROVED_CORPUS` leaf the owner commits by hand. But it means the `custom-content` edge write slug has TWO client entry points with different downstream walls, and only one was mapped.

## Denominator ledger

**Assigned population:** the custom-content system — manifest + schemas + consumers arrays + field-level finite-semantics + lifecycle + dossier surfacing.

## Gaps

1. **op-but-no-exposure** — the entire B2 cluster (24 registered editable prose paths, `userEdits.js:63-104`) has store+domain writers and zero mounted editors; `rename-npc` (B5) is committable with a live dispatcher and no UI caller; manual `recordSnapshot` has no VersionsTab button despite the header promising it (`VersionsTab.jsx:8`).
2. **displayed-but-no-lever** — VersionsTab promises side-by-side diff, none rendered; PlotHooksTab renders an authorable-substrate projection read-only; Chronicle feed rows are not annotatable (acceptable for evidence class, recorded for completeness).
3. **no-recovery** — dossier notes (B3) are a whole-object overwrite with no history/undo; a mis-save destroys prior notes permanently. Cheapest cure: fold dossierNotes into the versionHistory snapshot payload or keep a one-deep previous copy.
4. **no-provenance / partial-exposure receipt** — `rulesetLog` receipts are written and load-bearing (rumor seeding floor); the CHANGE is announced (a `ruleset_change` Herald entry) but the receipt's detail — per-key from/to and coercions — has no reader [corrected-by-verifier: was "rendered nowhere"]. `pipelineHistory` (§A17) is a registered `receiptRef` that is wiped on every regenerate and never persisted.
5. **HAZARD:history-regen-loss (open, documented)** — history reroll destroys authored history prose, siegeNarrative, legacyAnnotations, and worldPulse campaignEra entries (`settlementSlice.js:1043-1064`); owner-gated design ruling. Blocks safe exposure of the historicalEvent/currentTension members of B2.
6. **dead-code / fork risk** — `edit-prose` EDIT_KIND is declared, non-committable scaffolding (B6) while direct `_userEdits` writes serve the same need; two prose-edit substrates should converge under G-2b before more mounts land.
7. **evidence loss by tier (recorded, disclosed)** — free-tier chronicle rotation permanently discards full narrative snapshots past 5 entries (`chronicle.js:23-26`); disclosed in UI tooltip, so policy not bug.
8. **unknown-reach (minor)** — the gallery-description persistence RPC and the dossier-report moderation RPC were not read (marked PLAUSIBLE inline). `cappedVersionHistory` is now RESOLVED: cap 50 [corrected-by-verifier].
9. **undisclosed evidence loss [added-by-verifier]** — `campaign.chronicles` FIFO-drops past 24 entries (`campaignSlice.js:930`) with no UI disclosure, unlike the per-settlement chronicle whose rotation is disclosed in a chip tooltip. Same class as Gap 7, but hidden.

There are three: those two plus the DELIBERATE mirror pair `tableLedger.js` (B7, pendingEdits path) / `tableEvents.js` (B12, direct wizardNews path), whose fold decision is recorded and vetoable at `tableEvents.js:22-31` and guarded only by a value-identity parity test.

## Denominator ledger

Assigned population: history/chronicle/versions/receipts surfaces + every live prose writer, per the brief's entry-point list.

Enumeration method: `find`/`grep` for the six named tabs (both candidate directories — only `src/components/new/tabs/{Chronicle,History,Notes,PlotHooks,Rumors}Tab.jsx` + `src/components/settlement/VersionsTab.jsx` exist; import trace via `dossierLazyTabs.js` and `OutputContainer.jsx` confirms these are the live variants); `grep -rn EditableText src/components` (3 files → 1 live mount); `grep EditableInline` (1 live mount); `grep rollExplanations|rulesetLog|eventLog` across src; `grep queueEdit(` across components for queue-backed writers; `grep textarea|contenteditable` sweeps of flagged components (NotesTab, TableLedgerPanel, GalleryComments, GalleryDescriptionEditor, EventComposer, FeedbackWidget, AiAnalystPanel, InterviewPanel).

Count: 23 subject rows covering 12 evidence surfaces + 11 writer rows (B2 is a 24-member cluster; every member named).
**[corrected-by-verifier-2] Revised count: 34 subject rows — 19 evidence surfaces (A1-A19) + 15 writer rows (B1-B15), where B14 covers two mounts rather than one.** **[amended-by-critic-pass: 34 → 35 — A20 (`eventNarrativeSnapshots`) added; 20 evidence surfaces.]** The first verifier's 32 still under-counted: a `wizardNews`/`eventLog` census run by CALLEE across `src/domain` and `src/store` (rather than by component) surfaces `regionalGraph.eventLog` (§A18), and an importer census of the map components surfaces `pulseUndoStack`/`UndoHistoryPanel` (§A19) — the record that decides whether anything in §A is reversible.

**[superseded] First verifier's count: 32 subject rows — 17 evidence surfaces (A1-A17) + 15 writer rows (B1-B15).** The mapper's enumeration method was scoped to `src/components` + the six named dossier tabs, so it missed (a) every CAMPAIGN-level record (`campaign.chronicles`, the Chronicler's Letter, AdvanceReport), (b) two session-scoped receipt arrays that never surfaced under the six-tab grep (`pendingEditReceipts`, `pipelineHistory`), (c) the V-17 Campaign Import writer, (d) two writers outside the flagged component list (`GalleryReportDialog`, the PDF `NotesField`), and (e) the wizardNews wipe op. Independent terms that found them: `grep -n '[a-zA-Z]*\(History\|Log\|Ledger\|Receipt\|Digest\|Chronicles\?\)\s*:' src/store/*.js`; `ls src/components/map/`; `grep -rln '<textarea\|contentEditable' src`; `grep -rn 'EditableText' src` UNSCOPED (which is what exposed the second, PDF-side primitive of the same name).

Deliberately dispositioned OUT of population (boundary calls, not omissions):

The drift is concentrated in rows written from a file's own prose (headers, design comments) rather than from its call sites — which is also exactly where both refuted claims live.

**Standing methodological note for the remaining atlas slices.** Three of this slice's five substantive errors would have been caught by one habit: before recording a surface as *exposed*, grep its importers; before recording a record as *irreversible*, grep the undo/restore paths that write it. Neither is expensive, and both are cheaper than a G-program wave scoped against a wrong map.

## Gaps

1. **doctrine-conflict / dual-writer (sharpest finding): two divergent NPC/faction rename lanes.** Library lane (SettlementsPanel.applyRename, SettlementsPanel.jsx:331-392) matches NPCs by id, factions by name on `settlement.factions`, and cascades through relationships + cross-save interSettlementRelationships + ai_data. Store lane (settlementSlice.js:1262-1299, replayed by pendingEdits 'rename-npc', settlementPendingEdits.js:224) matches by INDEX, resolves factions on `powerStructure.factions` (the canonical list the library lane never touches), and cascades NOTHING — no relationships, no cross-save, no ai_data. A rename through one lane is invisible to the other's reference set. operationRegistry.js:122-123 claims both "carry the new name through references" — true only of the library lane. CONFIRMED. [added-by-verifier — the divergence is WORSE than stated, and the recommendation was backwards:] (a) the library lane's faction write lands on the LEGACY mirror only, which propagate.js:439-441 and settlementSlice.js:1282-1285 both identify as usually-empty for generator output — so for a generated settlement the library lane's faction rename is a NO-OP on the canonical list; (b) it writes only `.name`, never `.faction`, so `nameOf` (rulingPower.js:96-98, `.faction` first) keeps the old name even when the mirror IS populated; (c) SettlementDetailEditNames.jsx:84 iterates `settlement.factions`, so the Factions section of Edit Names renders EMPTY on a generated settlement and the door does not exist at all. The correct convergence takes the STORE lane's list resolution + dual-write and the LIBRARY lane's cascade — not "the library lane" wholesale.
1b. **op-but-no-exposure (faction half) [added-by-verifier]: there is NO working faction-rename door for a generated settlement.** The store lane's `renameFaction` has no caller (Gap 2) and the library lane's UI lists a list that is empty for generated saves (above). CONFIRMED by reading both surfaces; the user-visible consequence is that faction renaming is effectively unreachable on modern saves. Owner-visible, not a fix to make unasked.
2. **dead-code: store `renameFaction` has no caller** (settlementSlice.js:1277). The registry row advertises an op no surface exposes. CONFIRMED — independently re-derived by the verifier with `grep -rn "renameFaction" src/`: the only src hits are the definition, a cross-reference comment (settlementSlice.js:1008), the helpers-module note (settlementRenameHelpers.js:13), the registry, the GENERATED compendium mirror (compendiumData.generated.js:159), and the AI change-type classifier (narrativeMutations.js:31). Live callers exist only in tests (tests/store/settlementSlice.test.js:625,635,642; tests/store/editActionPersist.test.js:112) — so the tests keep a dead op green.
3. **unknown-reach: settlement rename does not cascade cross-save name-keyed references.** renameSettlementImpl (settlementRenameHelpers.js:69-138, read in full) touches only its own save + active slice, while other saves reference this settlement BY NAME (`relationship.partnerSettlement === detail.settlement.name`, SettlementsPanel.jsx:350; helpers.js:99). After a town rename, partner saves still carry the old name — and applyRename's cross-save NPC-rename match keys on the CURRENT name, so it would then skip those stale rows. CONFIRMED for the writer's non-cascade; PLAUSIBLE that no other path reconciles (none found).
4. **no-provenance: NPC/faction renames and all cosmetic map edits leave no receipt.** Only the canon-phase settlement rename writes a chronicle line; every op in this slice has receiptRef:null / undoToken:null in operationRegistry. Draft-phase renames vanish without trace. CONFIRMED.
5. **no-recovery (session-bounded): the map-edit undo/redo stack is session-only state** (useTownMapPresentation.js:81-145) — after reload the only recovery is Reset (destroys ALL cosmetic edits at once) or manual re-edit. Per-key revert exists (each with* op clears), but no persisted history. CONFIRMED.
6. **op-but-no-exposure: renameNPC reachable only through the pendingEdits queue replay**; no direct UI verb outside the live-editor queue lane. CONFIRMED.
7. **OWNER-DECISION (recorded, deliberately NOT recommended): joining the scene and canonical address spaces.** sceneSemantics.js:1-9 keeps them separate by constitutional intent; wiring neighbour-name approach labels to Realm ids beyond the existing explicit-id path, or minting district→faction identity from profile-layer inference (:325-328), is an owner call. Related owner-gated adjacents from memory: compendium deep-link scheme, terrain-at-cursor.

## Verification

Adversarial verification pass, 2026-07-26, worktree `.claude/worktrees/minifold`, branch `claude/composite-r4` (verified with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` before any read). Repo treated as read-only; the only file written is this one.

**Method.** Every one of the mapper's 18 rows was sampled — no row was taken on trust — spanning all interaction classes present in the slice (influenceable ×3, presentational ×10, authorable ×1, structural ×3, inspect-only ×1). For each row I re-opened the cited authority file and re-derived the claim from source, then attacked it on five axes: wrong class, wrong authority file, phantom operation, wrong gating, wrong recovery, and — most productive here — *evidence lines that do not say what is claimed*. ### canonize / uncanonize — the phase transition and its declared inverse [added-by-verifier]
- class: actionable (lifecycle phase mutation with a registry-declared undo token)
- authority: src/store/settlementSlice.js:1384-1418 (canonize), :1423-1435 (uncanonize); registered ops operationRegistry.js:65-66 — `canonize.undoToken:'uncanonize'` and `uncanonize.undoToken:'canonize'`, a mutually-declared reversible pair; save-scoped sibling `canonizeSavedSettlement` (:68, impl settlementRenameHelpers.js:227)
- operations: canonize() / uncanonize()
- preconditions: none (neither guards on the current phase)
- timing: immediate; persisted via persistActiveSaveLifecycle (:1391, :1432)
- scope: settlement lifecycle (phase + eventLog + canonizedAt)
- reach: canonize sets phase='canon', **empties eventLog**, stamps canonizedAt (:1387-1389); uncanonize sets phase='draft', **empties eventLog**, nulls canonizedAt (:1426-1428); both persist the whole lifecycle to the active save
- recovery: **NONE for the timeline.** The registry advertises the pair as each other's undo token, but the "undo" does not restore what the forward op destroyed — `uncanonize` discards the entire canon event log irreversibly, and re-`canonize` cannot bring it back (it empties the log again). No snapshot is taken on either side. This is the sharpest untracked no-recovery path in the slice and it is the one the mapper's Part (b) `revertToSnapshot` row gestures at ("canonizedAt is NOT restored") without naming its owner.
- provenance: CANON_PHASE_CHANGED analytics both ways; researchCapture 'canonized' fingerprint; generation-id 'canonize' milestone (:1409-1417)
- exposure: dossier canonize control / Settlements list canonize-by-id
- destination: dock (a phase change is the biggest commit in the product and deserves the Change Dock's confirm + receipt)
- surveyor: prohibited — silently destroys a campaign timeline
- maturity: built (destructive)
- status: CONFIRMED
- evidence: settlementSlice.js:1384-1435; src/store/operationRegistry.js:65-66,68
- notes/gaps: registry-declared undoToken that is NOT an undo = a legibility/contract defect of exactly the shape Gap 10 names for EDIT_POLICY; nothing pins undoToken semantics against real reversibility.

## Gaps

1. **op-but-no-exposure** — recordSnapshot has zero manual UI callers; VersionsTab's header promises "manual snapshot on demand + every Nth commit," neither wired (VersionsTab.jsx:8,:11; `grep -rn recordSnapshot src/`). The timeline can only grow via pending-edit auto-commits (settlementPendingEdits.js:482) and pre-revert autosnapshots (settlementSlice.js:576) — those are its only two product callers. [verifier note: correct as written here; the Part (a) row's stronger "ONLY product caller" phrasing was the error.]
2. **no-recovery** — regenSection takes NO pre-regen snapshot (settlementSlice.js:1037 feeds only the delta card); a draft NPC reroll of non-authored content is irreversible; history regen is the documented worst case.
3. **displayed-but-no-lever / partial restore** — revertToSnapshot restores settlement content but not phase/eventLog/canonizedAt; the VersionsTab timeline DISPLAYS canonize/export/edit milestones as if part of one restorable history while only snapshots revert (VersionsTab.jsx:70-106).
4. **dead-code** — buildRegenerationPlan (regenerationMode.js:85) has test-only importers (tests/domain/regenerationMode.test.js:9, tests/domain/b07DomainSchemaFixes.test.js:15; zero src importers — re-CONFIRMED by grep); flushSuppressPersist is read at **5** sites [corrected-by-verifier: was "4 sites" — settlementSlice.js:1487, :2226; fogEditBody.js:51; settlementRenameHelpers.js:43, :136] but set nowhere in src (dormant change-queue seam); clearSessionCommandJournal has no src caller (logout never clears the command journal).
5. **no-provenance (durable)** — pendingEditReceipts are session-only and capped at 100; the receipts that carry undoTokens and 'queued' world-order acknowledgments do not survive reload (settlementSlice.js:454-457). GAME_GRADE_PROGRAM.md:46 already names persisted receipts as G-1's deferred half.
6. **doctrine-conflict (minor)** — snapshot ids embed Math.random into the PERSISTED versionHistory envelope (settlementSlice.js:512), against the repo's own "never Math.random in persisted state" mapEdits doctrine; blob-adjacent, not sim-state, but the same class the pendingEdits id fix cured (pendingEdits.js:91-96).
7. **unknown-reach (invariant by convention)** — cross-save pendingEdits isolation relies on every reader filtering by ownerKey rather than physical removal; a future reader that forgets selectPendingEditOwnerScope re-opens SED-11. No single-writer scan pins this.
8. **asymmetric session durability** — pausedAdvance rehydrates across reload but pulseUndoStack / draft snapshots / draft pending edits / command journal **/ mapUndoStack + mapRedoStack / livingCatchUp / advanceInFlight** do not; users get no signal about which safety nets survive a refresh. [extended-by-verifier: the map undo stack is the largest omission — it is the product's only redo, is capped at 30, and dies silently on reload.]
9. **two writers for ai_data** — aiSlice direct writes bypass the outbox lane (outbox.js:22-25, recorded deferral).
10. **EDIT_POLICY↔dispatch parity unpinned** — the closed policy table (timing/class/adapter ids) is metadata beside hard-coded dispatch in applyOne/applyEditOp; totality is pinned in tests (pendingEdits.js:63-64) but policy-vs-writer semantic drift is not.
11. **[added-by-verifier] undoToken semantics unpinned** — `operationRegistry` declares an `undoToken` per op (`canonize`↔`uncanonize`, `commitPendingEdits`→`revertToSnapshot`, `recordSnapshot`→`revertToSnapshot`), and that field is exported into the generated compendium the user reads (compendiumData.generated.js:100-109). Nothing checks that the named token actually reverses the op. `uncanonize` is a live counter-example: it is declared as canonize's undo and it destroys the event log. Same shape as Gap 10, but this table is user-visible.
12. **[added-by-verifier] writer/reader field-name split in the version timeline** — recordSnapshot writes `settlement` (settlementSlice.js:518); buildVersionTimeline reads `snapshot` (VersionsTab.jsx:65) and the header documents the reader's name (:10). Inert today, but it is the exact substrate the promised side-by-side diff would be built on, and a diff built against the documented name would silently read `undefined` for every entry.
13. **[added-by-verifier] two recovery philosophies in one product** — the custom-content lane has append-only revisions with expected-head CAS and a non-destructive rollback (customContentSliceRuntime.js:561-599), while the settlement lane has snapshot-or-nothing with three irreversible verbs (regenSection('history'), uncanonize, removeSavedSettlement). Nothing reconciles them; a user who learns "rollback is safe" in the Workshop carries a false model into the dossier.
14. **[added-by-verifier] silently-swallowed world-side compensation** — undoLastEvent's crisis-twin withdraw and relationship-ripple reversal are both wrapped in bare `catch { /* world reconciliation is best-effort */ }` (settlementSlice.js:2022, :2039). A local undo can report success while the campaign world keeps the twin. No receipt, no analytics, no user signal.

## Verification

**Verifier pass — 2026-07-26, adversarial, against the LIVE minifold worktree** (`claude/composite-r4` @ `59f76448`, tree confirmed by `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` before any read). Repo treated as read-only; no git state was mutated.

**Method.** (1) Read the slice in full. (2) Sampled **all 23** original Part (a) rows — not the 12 minimum — because every row carried line-precise cites, and re-derived each load-bearing claim by reading the cited source region rather than grepping for the cited string. Full reads: `domain/pendingEdits.js`, `domain/pendingEditIntents.js`, `store/settlementPendingEdits.js`, `store/settlementPendingEditActions.js`, `store/settlementPendingEditWriters.js`, `components/settlement/VersionsTab.jsx`; targeted region reads across `store/settlementSlice.js` (lines 330-670, 690-1200, 1440-1660, 1660-1940, 1939-2180, 2200-2272), `generators/generateSettlementPipeline.js:210-373`, `store/campaignWorldPulseSlice.js`, `store/campaignPulseHelpers.js`, `store/campaignSlice.js`, `store/outbox.js`, `store/campaignSliceShared.js`, `store/index.js`, `store/persistMerge.js`, `store/mapSlice.js`, `store/customContentSliceRuntime.js`, `store/aiSlice.js`, `domain/userEdits.js`, `domain/canonStatus.js`, `domain/regenerationPolicy.js`, `domain/regenerationPreservation.js`, `application/commands/sessionCommandRuntime.js`, `application/commands/pendingEditCommitRuntime.js`, `components/dossier/SettlementWorkbench.jsx`, and the headers of `lib/saves.js`, `lib/pendingSaveDraft.js`, `lib/worldExport.js`, `lib/accountImport.js`, `store/galleryImportSettlement.js`, `store/canonEventCommandTransaction.js`, `store/campaignDeletionSession.js`, `store/fogEditBody.js`. (3) Attacked the denominator from two independent entry points the mapper did not use — the `operationRegistry.js` manifest and a recovery-verb regex over `src/store/` — rather than re-running its identifier grep.

**Counts.** 23 rows checked (100% of Part a) + all 10 Part (b) rows + all 15 Part (c) rows. **Confirmed: 21 of 23** rows substantively sound. **Refuted or downgraded: 9 distinct claims** across 8 rows. **10 members added.** No row was found to be wholly fabricated: every mechanism the mapper named exists and behaves as described in substance.

**What the mapper got right, and it matters.** The hard architectural claims all survived independent re-derivation: the owner-fence chain across the lazy module boundary, the pre-batch-snapshot-before-first-writer ordering, the disjoint-target rebase rule, the preview==apply staleness law, the persist triple, the outbox's owner-scoped mirror and crash-replay normalization, the canon-command CAS ordering, and the `revertToSnapshot` partial-restore correction (phase/eventLog/canonizedAt not restored) — which is the single most valuable finding in the document and is exactly right.

**The systematic defect: line-cite drift in one cluster.** Every regeneration-cluster address was wrong by a consistent offset (pipeline cites low by 59-76 lines; canonStatus by 1-5; preservation by 30-70), while the surrounding prose was accurate. That pattern reads as cites carried forward from an earlier revision of those files rather than re-derived at map time. The claims stand; the addresses did not, and an atlas whose value is navigability cannot ship stale coordinates. All corrected in place.

**Sharpest thing the denominator missed:** `uncanonize`. The operation registry advertises it to the user, through the generated compendium, as canonize's undo token — and it empties the entire canon event log with no snapshot, in both directions. A slice titled *lifecycle-recovery* that maps eleven recovery mechanisms and omits the one destructive lifecycle verb the product labels "reversible" has a hole where its sharpest finding should be.

**Verdict: SOUND WITH CORRECTIONS.** Trust the mechanism prose. Re-derive any line number in the regeneration cluster before navigating by it. Treat the population as ~30 members, not 23, and use `operationRegistry.js` as the denominator next time.

## Per-entity-family migration readiness

- **NPC family — READIEST.** The edit spine (queue→admission→review→commit→receipt→snapshot-undo) is complete and verified to the line; the Entity Inspector + ChangeDock exist flag-off; regen preservation is fixed in-tree (CONFLICT 1, uncommitted). Blockers before freeze: the named-fate owner ruling (queue #2), three unmounted committable kinds (#1 of workbench gaps), consent-barrier extension, and the session-only receipt tier.
- **Power/faith — mechanisms strong, edges weak.** Handlers and gates verified; but faction rename has no working door, 24/25 authored-prose paths are phantom, the deity pool owner-gate blocks any `deity:core:`-based work, and the deity second lane has asymmetric gating. Freeze the matrix only after queue #13/#14.
- **Economy — read-ready, verb-poor.** All read surfaces classify cleanly to inspector; the gap is the VERB SET (Services/Resources/institution cards have zero contextual verbs today), plus the two-ledger provenance split and the post-event stale-derivation window. The Workbench shell already recognizes `institution`; G-2b's work here is verbs, not homes.
- **Custom content — strongest write discipline, weakest ground.** Fingerprinted plans, CAS, confirmed-only persistence, append-only revisions — the model the rest should converge on — but the ENTIRE system is uncommitted and the cloud cutover is unrehearsed (queue #23). Factions bucket is authorable-but-inert (queue #24). Do not schedule G-2b migration on this family until the commit + cutover gates clear.
- **Presentation/scene — canvas archetype.** `applyMapEdit`/fog are the model direct-manipulation verbs; blockers: rename-lane convergence (queue #14), session-only undo, and the unwired arch/ kernel (program state, not this atlas's to schedule).
- **Derived/influenceable — inspector-only by law.** No destination work needed; but G9/G10 (queue #3) must land BEFORE any band word is frozen into G-2b copy, or the new surfaces will inherit inverted truth.
